articles.headline: U.S. levies new 25% tariff on Indian goods citing excess capacity
articles.title: U.S. announces new 25% tariffs on India, second-highest in the 14 countries against which action has been taken
articles.summary: The United States government announced a 25% import tariff on Indian goods on November 25, 2026, citing structural excess capacity that burdens American commerce. According to the Office of the U.S. Trade Representative, the rate could drop to 17% if a trade agreement is reached. The Indian Ministry of Commerce and Industry stated it is examining the notice while bilateral negotiations continue.
articles.description: The order by the U.S. Trade Representative also opens the door for a lower 17% tariff if India and the U.S. sign a trade deal

articles.headline: Judges recommend prosecutors end corruption case against Netanyahu
articles.title: Judges recommend prosecutors end corruption case against Netanyahu
articles.description: Israeli judges have ruled there is little prospect Benjamin Netanyahu will be convicted of corruption.

articles.headline: Two Italian technicians killed by Iranian strike in Kuwait
articles.title: Two Italians killed in strike in Kuwait, as Iran denies responsibility
articles.summary: Two Italian nationals working as technicians for German firm Rheinmetall died following an explosion caused by a drone attack on a facility in Kuwait, according to Italy's foreign ministry. Kuwait's defence ministry reported the casualties resulted from falling shrapnel after intercepting Iranian drones, while Iran denied responsibility for any offensive operations during the ongoing regional conflict involving U.S. forces.
articles.description: The pair were technicians for German company Rheinmetall, according to Italy's foreign ministry.

articles.headline: Refinery attack in Saudi Arabia kills worker and halts operations
articles.title: Attack on Saudi’s Jazan refinery kills one person, disrupts operations
articles.summary: An aerial projectile struck an oil refinery in Jazan, Saudi Arabia, on Thursday, killing a Nepali worker and injuring others while causing a fire and temporary operational disruptions, according to the Ministry of Energy. The Saudi-led military coalition blamed the Iranian-backed Houthi movement for the strike and responded by destroying a missile launch platform in Hodeidah, Yemen.
articles.description: The attack killed a Nepali national, injured several people and sparked a fire, Saudi Energy Ministry says.

articles.headline: Centre proposes special parliamentary session to run from November 30 to December 3
articles.title: Amended Delimitation Bill likely to be tabled in special Parliament sitting from November 30
articles.summary: Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju announced that the Lok Sabha will convene on November 30 and the Rajya Sabha on December 2, with both houses concluding on December 3, 2026. According to the minister, the special sitting aims to transact essential government business while the Monsoon Session remains unprorogued, keeping alive speculation about constitutional amendments linked to the Women’s Reservation Bill.
articles.description: Centre announces special sitting of Parliament from November 30, 2026, over 100 days since both Houses were adjourned without prorogation; government trying to pass the Bill after ‘operation lotus’, says Congress

articles.headline: Winter storms displace thousands of Palestinians in Gaza tents
articles.title: Why are winter rains forcing Palestinians in Gaza to flee again?
articles.summary: Heavy November rains flooded roughly 70,000 tents across Gaza within twelve hours, affecting over 226,000 people and forcing hundreds to relocate again, according to United Nations figures. The storms and subsequent infrastructure failures caused multiple fatalities while worsening health risks, as shelter supplies remained stalled at borders due to Israeli restrictions.
articles.description: Israeli restrictions on humanitarian aid, damaged buildings and flooded tents leave displaced Palestinians vulnerable.

articles.headline: Federal judge blocks administration restrictions on birthright citizenship
articles.title: Judge strikes down Trump’s latest restrictions on US birthright citizenship
articles.summary: United States District Court Judge Christopher Cooper ruled on Wednesday to block the administration's policy denying birthright citizenship to certain children born to non-citizen parents. The decision marks another legal setback for executive orders attempting to restrict constitutional citizenship guarantees previously upheld by the Supreme Court in landmark rulings.
articles.description: After a Supreme Court ruling against it, the Trump administration had tried a narrower set of restrictions.

articles.headline: What will Trump’s latest tariffs mean for the world?
articles.title: What will Trump’s latest tariffs mean for the world?
articles.description: New measures come after previous trade tariffs ruled illegal.

articles.headline: Kushner explains the ‘good thing’ about Gaza’s destruction
articles.title: Kushner explains the ‘good thing’ about Gaza’s destruction
articles.description: Jared Kushner says the “good thing” about Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza is that it can be built into “something new”.

articles.headline: Trump demands investigation into US economic growth data released prior to midterms
articles.title: Trump calls GDP data released before midterms ‘fake’, demands investigation
articles.summary: Former United States President Donald Trump demanded a federal investigation into revised third-quarter gross domestic product figures released by the Department of Commerce, alleging without evidence that the initial data were intentionally manipulated before the November 3 elections. The Bureau of Economic Analysis revised annualized growth up to 4.3 percent from 3.4 percent. Officials routinely update statistics as complete source data becomes available.
articles.description: President says it was a deliberate decision to release 'fake' growth numbers before US midterm elections.

articles.headline: EU leaders debate long-term budget and financial aid for Ukraine
articles.title: EU leaders struggle to agree on long-term budget, $49bn Ukraine loan
articles.summary: European Union leaders gathered in Brussels for an extraordinary summit to negotiate a nearly $1.76 trillion budget proposal for 2028 to 2034 alongside a $49 billion loan for Ukraine. Divisions emerged as some officials advocated for fiscal restraint while others prioritized defense and funding. Securing unanimous approval remains uncertain amid upcoming national elections across several member states.
articles.description: The bloc is holding an extraordinary summit in Brussels to discuss its budget proposal for 2028 to 2034.

articles.headline: Saudi-led coalition launches airstrikes on Houthi-held Sanaa
articles.title: Yemen's Houthi-held capital hit after group targets Riyadh
articles.summary: The Saudi-led coalition conducted retaliatory airstrikes against Houthi-held territory in Yemen, including the capital city of Sanaa, after intercepting ballistic missiles targeting Riyadh. The military exchanges follow a recent escalation in Yemen's revived civil war, which resumed in July following the breakdown of a multi-year truce, causing extensive damage and rising casualties across the region.
articles.description: The exchanges between the Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen have become near-daily in the country's revived civil war

articles.headline: India and UAE agree to accelerate joint defense equipment production
articles.title: India, UAE to accelerate joint development and production of next generation defence equipment
articles.summary: India and the United Arab Emirates agreed to boost co-development and co-production partnerships in next-generation military equipment during the fourteenth meeting of their Joint Defence Cooperation Committee in Abu Dhabi. Co-chaired by Indian Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh and UAE Under Secretary Lieutenant General Ibrahim Nasser M. Al Alawi, the talks advanced bilateral defense ties.
articles.description: Meeting provided strategic direction to initiatives under the India-UAE Strategic Defence Partnership Framework, signed during PM’s May visit to the UAE

articles.headline: Supreme Court rules PMLA property attachment benches need judicial members
articles.title: PMLA Bench adjudicating property attachment must have at least one judicial member: Supreme Court
articles.summary: India's Supreme Court ruled that benches adjudicating property attachments under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act must include at least one judicial member. Chief Justice Surya Kant delivered the judgment, emphasizing that legal expertise is required to evaluate civil rights before the state can confiscate assets suspected of constituting proceeds from criminal activities.
articles.description: The PMLA permits the State to reach into a citizen’s estate even before guilt is proved, the Supreme Court notes

articles.headline: Israeli airstrikes in Gaza kill nine people including Khaled Abu Nada
articles.title: Israel kills nine in Gaza, including Hamas-appointed deputy Education Minister, officials say
articles.summary: Israeli airstrikes and gunfire killed at least nine Palestinians in the Gaza Strip, including Hamas-appointed deputy education minister Khaled Abu Nada. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu confirmed the targeted killing as part of ongoing military operations against Hamas officials. Palestinian and Israeli tallies indicate that thousands have died since a ceasefire was established in October 2025.
articles.description: Medics said an Israeli airstrike hit an apartment in Deir Al-Balah in central Gaza Strip, killing ‌Khaled Abu Nada, the Deputy Gaza Education Minister, and his wife.

articles.headline: Nvidia halts AI server shipments to four Southeast Asian nations
articles.title: Nvidia stops shipping AI servers to four Southeast Asian nations
articles.summary: U.S. tech company Nvidia instructed manufacturing partners to stop shipping computer servers containing artificial intelligence chips to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia, according to the Financial Times. The reported halt on November 26, 2026, follows tightened U.S. export controls aimed at cracking down on chip smuggling and the grey market renting computing power to Chinese entities, significantly impacting regional data centre operations.
articles.description: The Financial Times report said Nvidia had instructed manufacturing partners to stop shipping computer servers to buyers in Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia

articles.headline: Kremlin accuses Ukraine of trying to widen conflict to seas
articles.title: Kremlin accuses Ukraine of trying to widen conflict zone to Mediterranean and Baltic seas
articles.summary: The Kremlin claimed on November 26, 2026, that Ukraine is attempting to expand its war into the Mediterranean and Baltic seas through terrorist activities, calling the actions very dangerous. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov responded to a joint U.S. and NATO statement urging restraint, following recent Ukrainian drone strikes that hit a Russian naval corvette in Libya and a cargo ship in the Gulf of Finland.
articles.description: Ukraine sank a Russian naval corvette in a Libyan port using maritime drones on Sunday, a day after ​it carried out a ‌drone strike on a Russian military-linked cargo ship in the Gulf of Finland

articles.headline: President Murmu calls pending court cases a major justice challenge
articles.title: Pendency a challenge to justice delivery, says President
articles.summary: Indian President Droupadi Murmu stated on November 26, 2026, that the high volume of pending court cases creates a major challenge for the nation's justice delivery system and hinders timely verdicts. Speaking at Supreme Court Constitution Day celebrations, she noted judicial efforts involving technology and special courts, while Chief Justice Surya Kant emphasised ongoing initiatives to ensure broader access for citizens.
articles.description: At the Constitution Day celebrations organised by the Supreme Court, President Murmu listed measures used to improve timely delivery of justice

articles.headline: Myanmar president rejects international court genocide orders
articles.title: Myanmar says it will not fully comply with ICJ genocide orders
articles.summary: Myanmar's military-backed president Min Aung Hlaing stated on November 26, 2026, that his administration will not fully comply with UN International Court of Justice measures. The court previously ruled that security forces committed genocide against the Rohingya minority during 2017 operations in Rakhine state. The crackdown displaced over 730,000 people to Bangladesh, according to records.
articles.description: The ruling by ‌the ⁠ICJ, the first instance of the UN court holding a ⁠state responsible for genocide, is final but the court has very limited options to enforce it

articles.headline: Two Italians killed by drone strike debris in Kuwait facility
articles.title: Two Italians killed by ‘drone strike debris’ in Kuwait
articles.summary: Two Italian technicians working at an air-defence surveillance station in Kuwait died from injuries sustained after being hit by falling debris during an Iranian drone interception. Kuwait's Ministry of Defence reported that two other workers, a Kuwaiti and a Pakistani national, were wounded in the incident at a vital site, while Iranian state media quoted military officials denying any offensive operations in the region.
articles.description: Iran has strongly denied any involvement in the fatal incident.

articles.headline: European Union leaders appoint Pablo Hernandez de Cos as next European Central Bank chief
articles.title: Spanish economist to become new European Central Bank chief
articles.summary: European Union leaders have appointed Pablo Hernandez de Cos as the next head of the Frankfurt-based European Central Bank, succeeding Christine Lagarde in February. The fifty-five-year-old Spaniard, currently heading the Bank for International Settlements, will become the first person from his country to lead the institution. Diplomats praise his pragmatism as he assumes the role during a challenging period for the eurozone economy.
articles.description: Economist Pablo Hernandez de Cos was announced after a meeting of eurozone leaders.

articles.headline: U.K. net migration falls to lowest level since 1997
articles.title: U.K. net migration falls to lowest since 1997; Indians largest foreign group entering and leaving the country
articles.summary: Official U.K. government figures released on November 26, 2026, show net migration dropped to 77,000, driven largely by a decline in non-European Union arrivals. Indians constituted the largest foreign nationality group both immigrating and emigrating. The dramatic decrease follows stricter policies implemented after record highs during the administration of Boris Johnson.
articles.description: Some 44,000 Indians arrived in the U.K. for work-related reasons, 77,000 to study, and 5,000 for other reasons. Some 28,000 Indians on work visas left the U.K. and 55,000 on study visas departed

articles.headline: Two dead after Iranian drone attack on Kuwait
articles.title: Two dead after Iranian drone attack on Kuwait
articles.description: Kuwait’s army says two Italian workers were killed and four others were injured in an Iranian drone attack.

articles.headline: UK and EU to publish post-Brexit trade and emissions treaties
articles.title: New UK-EU treaty has 10-year termination clause
articles.summary: The British government and the European Union plan to release two post-Brexit treaties covering food exports and carbon trading on Thursday. The food export agreement includes a ten-year termination clause requiring infrastructure rebuilding costs if ended. European affairs minister Hamish Falconer stated the measures will eliminate paperwork and reduce business expenses, although political figures have expressed differing views on the arrangement.
articles.description: Text of the treaties was published this afternoon, alongside legislation designed to enact the bulk of the deal.

articles.headline: US Democrats weigh funding bill strategy to restrict military operations in Iran
articles.title: Can Trump continue with Iran war despite funding restrictions?
articles.summary: As federal funding approaches an expiration date on December 11, Democratic lawmakers are considering leveraging the upcoming budget package to pressure President Donald Trump by restricting offensive operations in the ongoing war on Iran. According to experts, while the measure could constrain executive spending, a potential presidential veto and existing Pentagon resources mean it may not immediately halt the conflict.
articles.description: A Congress budget bill could serve as a pressure tactic on Trump to end the war but could also trigger a shutdown.

articles.headline: Serbia schedules early presidential election for December 27 following former leader's departure
articles.title: Serbia sets Presidential election for December 27 after students won Parliamentary vote
articles.summary: Serbia's Parliament Speaker Aleksandar Cupic announced an early presidential vote for December 27 following the September resignation of former President Aleksandar Vucic. The upcoming election follows a student movement's victory over Mr. Vucic's party in an October 25 parliamentary ballot, concluding fourteen years of virtually unchallenged rule and prompting a surge in official detentions.
articles.description: The Presidential vote will be held after a student movement defeated Mr. Vucic's right-wing Serbian Progressive Party in an early Parliamentary ballot on October 25

articles.headline: China calls border situation stable following military talks with India
articles.title: Situation in India-China border areas remains ‘generally stable’, says China
articles.summary: The Chinese Defence Ministry stated that bilateral border regions remain generally stable after concluding high-level military discussions with India. Senior Colonel Chen Xi confirmed that both nations communicate through diplomatic and military channels to maintain peace. Meanwhile, recent Corps Commander-level talks focused on establishing engagement protocols along the frontier in Arunachal Pradesh before winter conditions set in.
articles.description: On November 24, 2026, India and China concluded a second round of Corps Commander-level talks aimed at easing tensions along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) in Arunachal Pradesh

articles.headline: United States proposes new trade tariffs against fourteen partners
articles.title: Are Trump’s tariffs aimed at securing US-friendly trade deals?
articles.summary: The administration of United States President Donald Trump proposed new trade tariffs ranging from 20 percent to 40 percent against 14 key trading partners, including China and India. Announced by the United States Trade Representative on Wednesday, the measures respond to alleged unfair trading practices and industrial overcapacity while serving as leverage in ongoing trade negotiations.
articles.description: New US policy threatens further tariff hikes on China, India, Vietnam if trade negotiations fall through.

articles.headline: Cheaper generic HIV prevention injection arrives in Africa
articles.title: Hope for millions as cheaper HIV prevention jab reaches Africa
articles.summary: Zambia received the first global shipment of a generic version of lenacapavir on Wednesday, with deliveries to Uganda expected soon. Administered twice a year, the injection costs approximately $40 annually per person. The Global Fund stated the rollout aims to expand access across low- and middle-income countries where sub-Saharan Africa bears the highest disease burden.
articles.description: Lenacapavir, administered as an injection twice a year, is nearly 100% effective at preventing HIV infection.

articles.headline: Supreme Court seeks response from Centre and protest organisers on demonstration rules
articles.title: Plea seeks guidelines to govern protests; Supreme Court issues notice to Centre, CJP leaders
articles.summary: The Supreme Court agreed to examine a petition filed by a lawyers body requesting standard operating procedures for public demonstrations. The Bench issued notices to the central government and political leaders following concerns regarding unauthorised protests held in Delhi earlier in the year. The petition emphasises balancing democratic dissent with public order and the protection of normal civic life.
articles.description: Supreme Court to examine plea for uniform protest guidelines; Centre, CJP leaders issued notice as demands SOPs to regulate demonstrations

articles.headline: Myanmar refuses to comply with parts of ICJ genocide ruling
articles.title: Myanmar refuses to comply with parts of ICJ genocide ruling
articles.summary: Leader Min Aung Hlaing announced that Myanmar will reject inappropriate requirements from the International Court of Justice ruling that found the country guilty of genocide. The landmark decision followed a 2017 military crackdown in Rakhine State that killed thousands of Rohingya Muslims and forced more than 700,000 to flee to Bangladesh.
articles.description: A landmark ruling by the International Court of Justice (ICJ) convicted Myanmar of genocide against its Rohingya minority.

articles.headline: Israeli air strikes in Gaza kill eight Palestinians including Hamas official
articles.title: Hamas political official and wife among eight Palestinians killed in Israeli strikes on Gaza
articles.summary: Three Israeli air strikes across the Gaza Strip on Thursday killed eight Palestinians, including Hamas political official Khaled Abu Nada and his wife in Deir al-Balah. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu confirmed the death on social media, stating that approximately 80 Hamas officials have been killed over the past month as military operations continue.
articles.description: The killings are the latest from a series of near daily attacks by Israel against what it says are Hamas targets.

articles.headline: Ukraine drone attack kills five in Russian-occupied Zaporizhia
articles.title: Ukraine drone attack kills five in Russian-occupied Zaporizhia
articles.summary: At least five individuals died and three sustained injuries during a Ukrainian drone strike targeting a parking facility in Vesioloye within Russian-occupied Zaporizhia, according to Moscow-installed governor Yevgeny Balitsky. Meanwhile, Russian ballistic missiles struck Kyiv, hitting a shopping center and damaging military-industrial installations. The ongoing conflict has severely degraded Ukraine's energy infrastructure since the full-scale invasion commenced in February 2022.
articles.description: Russian forces launch ballistic missile attack on Ukrainian capital Kyiv, hitting a shopping centre and other buildings.

articles.headline: State attorneys general attempt to block Character.AI data sale
articles.title: 42 state AGs are trying to stop Character.AI from selling users’ chats
articles.summary: A bipartisan group consisting of forty-two state attorneys general is working to prevent chatbot developer Character.AI from auctioning off private chat records belonging to more than twenty-one million accounts during its Chapter 11 bankruptcy proceedings. Officials raised concerns that the proposed sale of data originating from over two million minors lacks adequate privacy protections, user deletion options, or restrictions on subsequent buyers.
articles.description: A coalition of 42 state attorneys general is trying to prevent Character.AI from selling off user data as it navigates Chapter 11 bankruptcy proceedings. In a deluge of nearly identical press releases, the various AGs accuse the company of planning to auction off "the private chat histories of more than 21 million U.S. accounts - […]

articles.headline: US regulators approve SpaceX plan to deploy one million data satellites
articles.title: Musk's plan to send a million SpaceX data satellites into space approved
articles.summary: The Federal Communications Commission granted SpaceX permission to launch one million satellites into low-Earth orbit for space-based artificial intelligence data processing. FCC Chairman Brendan Carr endorsed the Starmind project as a technological advancement, while company owner Elon Musk expressed appreciation on social media. The initiative aims to alleviate terrestrial energy demands, though experts have raised concerns regarding space debris and orbital congestion.
articles.description: The Starmind constellation aims to be the most cost and energy-efficient way to meet the growing demand for AI computing power.

articles.headline: Highway fire near Cairo leaves thirty-one people dead
articles.title: Deadly fire erupts near Cairo killing dozens of people
articles.summary: A massive highway blaze in the Warraq neighborhood north of Cairo resulted in thirty-one fatalities and twenty-one injuries. State-owned media indicated the incident occurred when a high-voltage cable fell near a fuel tanker, causing the driver to lose control and overturn, which sprayed surrounding vehicles with petrol. Egypt's health ministry reported that the wounded individuals are receiving medical treatment at nearby hospitals.
articles.description: At least 31 people have died in a large fire on a busy highway in Cairo, after a fuel tanker overturned, says Egypt's health ministry.

articles.headline: Israeli strikes kill senior education official and others in Gaza
articles.title: Israeli attacks on Gaza kill senior education official, seven other people
articles.summary: Israeli air strikes across the Gaza Strip resulted in at least eight deaths, including Ministry of Education undersecretary Khaled Abu Nada and his wife in Deir el-Balah, according to local health officials. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defence Minister Israel Katz stated that Abu Nada was a Hamas figure. Gaza Health Ministry figures indicate that more than 1,600 Palestinians have died from attacks since a ceasefire took effect in October.
articles.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu confirms killing of Khaled Abu Nada, undersecretary of Education Ministry.

articles.headline: Elon Musk announces every US child will receive two SpaceX shares
articles.title: Elon Musk says every child in U.S. will get two SpaceX shares
articles.summary: SpaceX chief executive officer Elon Musk announced that every child in the United States will receive two shares of company stock, one issued by SpaceX and one matched personally by him. The initiative follows a prior contribution of Class A common stock to active Trump Accounts by the aerospace manufacturer, though specific lockup terms remain unconfirmed.
articles.description: SpaceX did ​not immediately respond ‌to a request for comment on whether Mr. Musk’s SpaceX share donations would be linked to Trump Accounts or ‌come with any kind of ​lockup period

articles.headline: Former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina plans return amid escalating political tensions
articles.title: Sheikh Hasina’s return gambit tests Bangladesh’s political fault lines
articles.summary: Former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina announced plans to end over two years of exile in India and return to Bangladesh on December 16, testing political fault lines. The interim administration and Bangladesh Nationalist Party officials stated she could only return as a convicted fugitive through extradition, while her Awami League party called for nationwide lockdowns.
articles.description: The ousted leader’s December 16 return plan has energised the Awami League leaders and cadre, tested Tarique Rahman’s government and complicated Dhaka’s efforts to reset ties with New Delhi

articles.headline: South African court overturns 2022 impeachment report against President Cyril Ramaphosa
articles.title: Cyril Ramaphosa wins court bid to overturn impeachment report
articles.summary: A South African high court ruled in favour of President Cyril Ramaphosa, setting aside a 2022 parliamentary panel report that alleged misconduct regarding a 2020 farmhouse theft. The court found the panel exceeded its remit and made legal errors. The ruling removes findings that previously threatened his political career and prompted ongoing legal battles.
articles.description: The 74-year-old leader was accused of hiding from police and tax authorities a 2020 break-in and theft of $580,000, which was stashed in furniture at his luxury Phala Phala farmhouse in the northern Limpopo province

articles.headline: DR Congo Ebola cases surpass 12,000 amid escalating eastern conflict
articles.title: DR Congo Ebola cases surpass 12,000 as fighting disrupts response in east
articles.summary: Confirmed Ebola infections in the Democratic Republic of the Congo exceeded 12,000, driven by conflict, delayed detection, and strained health services across eight provinces. According to government data and humanitarian workers, intensifying fighting in Ituri province between the Congolese army and the Convention for the Popular Revolution forced emergency evacuations and disrupted containment operations, heightening risks for millions.
articles.description: Authorities struggle to contain country's worst Ebola outbreak, as fighting in east displaces health workers, civilians.

articles.headline: India and China hold high-level talks on border management
articles.title: India, China hold high-level talks in Arunachal sector on border management, LAC issues: MEA
articles.summary: The Indian and Chinese armies conducted high-level discussions this month in the Arunachal Pradesh sector to address border management and Line of Actual Control issues, the Ministry of External Affairs stated on November 25, 2026. Led by Lt. Gen Girish Kalia for India, the talks aim to maintain peace following previous regional tensions.
articles.description: MEA spokesperson Randhir also addressed a report claiming China-sourced satellite data may have aided Pakistan in tracking Indian troop movements and monitoring installations during Operation Sindoor

articles.headline: Low postdoc funding drives Indian scientific brain drain overseas
articles.title: Low funding for postdoc roles fuelling brain drain, govt. funds only 2,500 positions
articles.summary: Indian-origin scientists are driving technological advancements at institutions such as MIT, Stanford, and Caltech due to systemic limitations in India's domestic research ecosystem. Young researchers in India face severe administrative hurdles, delayed scholarships, and rigid funding deadlines that contrast sharply with the multi-year grants and flexible environments available in the United States, according to an analysis published on September 11, 2026.
articles.description: India spends about $13 a year per person on research; China spends $250, the U.S. over $2,100. There are just 262 full-time-equivalent researchers per million people in the country

articles.headline: War and drought severely threaten agricultural livelihoods across Sudan
articles.title: War and drought threaten livelihoods of Sudan’s farmers
articles.summary: Decades-old farming communities in Sudan face unprecedented harvest failures due to a crippling water crisis driven by below-average rainfall and war-induced infrastructure destruction. Organizations like the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization and the International Committee of the Red Cross reported that electricity shortages, fuel scarcity, and damaged power stations have severely disrupted irrigation systems and threatened millions.
articles.description: Attacks on electricity infrastructure and drought are threatening Sudan's harvests and leaving millions without water.

articles.headline: Supreme Court quashes premature release of former MP Anand Mohan in murder case
articles.title: Supreme Court quashes premature release of former MP Anand Mohan in murder case
articles.summary: The Supreme Court quashed the premature release of former MP Anand Mohan, who was serving a life sentence for the 1994 murder of district magistrate G. Krishnaiah. Setting aside the Bihar government remission policy, the Bench directed Mohan to surrender within one month and mandated that the victim's wife be heard in future remission attempts.
articles.description: The apex court says Article 21 is not a “one-sided guarantee, equally encompasses victims, society at large

articles.headline: India records record 378 million tonnes of foodgrain production for 2025-26
articles.title: India produced record 378.53 million tonnes of foodgrains in 2025-26: Agriculture Minister
articles.summary: Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan released final crop estimates showing India produced a record 378.53 million tonnes of foodgrains in 2025-26, exceeding the previous year by 20.8 million tonnes. Rice production reached 155.15 million tonnes, maintaining India's position as the largest global producer ahead of China, while wheat output stood at 122.06 million tonnes.
articles.description: Shivraj Singh Chouhan also released the first advance estimates for the 2026–27 crop year, stating that output is expected to remain on track for the upcoming season despite El Niño and inadequate rainfall

articles.headline: Fuel tanker crash on Cairo Ring Road causes deadly fire
articles.title: Fuel tanker crash ignites massive fire on highway surrounding Cairo, killing at least 31 people
articles.summary: At least thirty people died and twenty-five others sustained injuries when a fuel tanker crash ignited a massive blaze on the Ring Road encircling Cairo on Wednesday, November 25, 2026. The Egyptian Health Ministry reported that the incident occurred in the densely populated Waraq area of Giza, charring numerous vehicles and prompting an ongoing investigation by the Public Prosecutor's office.
articles.description: The blaze on Ring Road, a key artery that encircles the Egyptian capital, also injured at least 25 people and left more than two dozen cars and motorcycles charred, the Public Prosecutor’s office said in a statement

articles.headline: India and the Netherlands upgrade bilateral ties to strategic partnership
articles.title: India, Netherlands upgrade ties; sign 17 MoUs on water, renewable energy, and semiconductors
articles.summary: During Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit on May 16 and 17, 2026, India and the Netherlands elevated their relations to a Strategic Partnership. Both nations signed 17 agreements covering water, agriculture, health, renewable energy, and critical minerals. According to Dutch media, Prime Minister Rob Jetten also raised sensitive topics including press freedoms, which the Ministry of External Affairs rejected.
articles.description: MEA pushes back on Dutch concerns over press freedom and minority rights in India. Agreements signed include a semiconductor fabrication project between TATA Electronics and Dutch company ASML

articles.headline: Gaza Ministry of Health declares epidemic alert following sharp surge in meningitis cases
articles.title: Gaza meningitis cases surge as collapsing infrastructure fuels health fears
articles.summary: The Gaza Ministry of Health declared an epidemic alert after reporting 272 meningitis cases in October, driven by collapsing infrastructure, severe overcrowding in displacement camps, and poor sanitation. Paediatricians at Rantisi Children Hospital noted a high volume of admissions for bacterial and viral infections, while international organizations reported critical shortages of laboratory supplies and medicines.
articles.description: Meningitis is raising alarm in Gaza, where overcrowding, damaged sanitation are putting children at risk.

articles.headline: US technology companies provide key infrastructure for Israeli military operations
articles.title: How Silicon Valley became central to Israel’s war on Palestinians
articles.summary: Major United States technology corporations including Amazon, Microsoft, Google, and Palantir supply advanced cloud computing, artificial intelligence, and facial recognition infrastructure to support Israeli military operations in Gaza and the West Bank. According to rights groups, leaked documents and UN reports, this technology facilitates intelligence gathering, communications interception, and automated targeting systems, leading to deep integration between US firms and former members of Israel's military cyberwarfare units.
articles.description: From surveillance systems to AI targeting, US tech giants are deeply embedded in Israel's war machine.

articles.headline: International Criminal Court judges face US sanctions over war crimes investigations
articles.title: ICC judge Kimberly Prost tries war crimes. She’s a target of US sanctions
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump's administration has imposed financial penalties, asset freezes, and visa restrictions on International Criminal Court judges, including Canadian jurist Kimberly Prost, and other officials. These sanctions stem from court investigations into alleged war crimes committed by US personnel and Israeli leadership in Gaza. The measures have disrupted the daily lives of judges, complicated international banking transactions, and threatened the operational capacity of the judicial institution.
articles.description: Apps not working. Bank transfers not going through. And a court fighting for international law must skirt US firms.

articles.headline: Imprisoned Iranian women face death sentences following anti-government protests
articles.title: Desperate appeals from women on death row in Iran after protests
articles.summary: Iranian twin sisters Taraneh and Romina Rahimi are among several women facing execution or lengthy prison terms following anti-government protests in January 2026. According to relatives and human rights groups, the defendants endured severe physical abuse and forced confessions during interrogation. The Iranian embassy in London categorically rejected allegations of torture and stated that legal penalties were issued for violent offenses.
articles.description: Female protesters and dissidents are being sentenced to death in numbers not seen for decades, a rights group says.

articles.headline: Origins and evolution of body mass index as obesity measure
articles.title: How waistlines, organ function tell a better story of obesity than BMI does
articles.summary: The body mass index originated in 1832 when Belgian astronomer Adolphe Quetelet sought to understand human populations using height and weight measurements. Originally known as the Quetelet Index, the ratio was renamed in 1972 by United States physiologist Ancel Keys after determining it best represented body fat, though it cannot distinguish between muscle mass and excess fat.
articles.description: In 2025, The Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinology established a commission of 58 experts from different countries to set obesity-related guidelines. A new study in Nature has tested whether the commission’s recommendations can actually distinguish between people at different levels of risk, with data from 8.4 lakh adults

articles.headline: Nepal initiates process to declare 213 missing Indian nationals presumed dead
articles.title: Nepal flash floods: Kathmandu begins process to declare 213 missing Indians presumed dead
articles.summary: The government of Nepal has started the official procedure to declare 213 Indian nationals missing since the August 26 flash floods presumed dead. According to the Indian Embassy in Nepal, the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority published the list on November 25, 2026, inviting public objections until December 2 before finalising death certificates. The devastating floods in the Trishuli-Bhote Koshi river system killed at least 1,453 people.
articles.description: Inviting objections or concerns, the Embassy said concerned family members could contact it via eoikathmandufloodsupport@gmail.com or +9779851316807

articles.headline: Brazil denounces proposed United States tariffs on aircraft and sugar
articles.title: Brazil blasts ‘unacceptable’ new US tariff proposals
articles.summary: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's administration has condemned unilateral tariff proposals announced by the United States trade representative targeting Brazilian manufactured aircraft and sugar imports. Brazil stated it is weighing reciprocal measures while remaining open to negotiated solutions through bilateral talks. The proposed duties, which could take effect in January, form part of a broader package impacting multiple trading partners following disputes over trade practices.
articles.description: President Lula’s office says Brazil will not yield to threats and aims for a negotiated resolution.

articles.headline: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un inspects nuclear facilities and urges expansion
articles.title: North Korea's Kim vows to build more nuclear weapons after ignoring Trump's overture
articles.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un inspected nuclear materials production facilities and called for the accelerated manufacturing of more nuclear weapons. Reported on November 26, 2026, by the Korean Central News Agency, the visit follows Kim ignoring recent diplomatic overtures from United States President Donald Trump. Kim stated that bolstering the nuclear arsenal is necessary to counter escalating security threats from the United States and South Korea.
articles.description: North Korea didn't say where the nuclear materials production factories that Kim Jong Un visited this week are located; U.S President Trump reiterated his eagerness to restore diplomacy with Mr. Kim as he visited China last week for the APEC summit

articles.headline: United States prepares to announce tariffs on global trading partners
articles.title: US announces new tariffs on host of countries including India
articles.summary: The United States is preparing to introduce new import taxes affecting at least fourteen jurisdictions, including China, the European Union, and Japan. The upcoming announcement follows a Section 301 investigation launched after the Supreme Court invalidated previous trade measures implemented by President Donald Trump. While the administration argues the tariffs will protect American manufacturing, critics contend the policy risks increasing consumer prices and escalating international trade tensions.
articles.description: The new levies would hit many of America's trading partners, including India.

articles.headline: Supreme Court issues notice to Delhi Police on bail pleas by activists
articles.title: Supreme Court issues notice on bail pleas by Umar Khalid, Sharjeel Imam in 2020 Delhi riots case
articles.summary: The Supreme Court issued notice on November 25, 2026, regarding interim bail petitions filed by activists Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam related to the 2020 Delhi riots. Both individuals have spent over six years in custody under the Unlawful Activities Prevention Act while awaiting trial for the violence that erupted during protests against the Citizenship Amendment Act.
articles.description: The court declined to take up their pleas for interim relief; CJI to set up three-judge Bench to decide whether prolonged incarceration and delay in trial can override stringent bail curbs under UAPA

articles.headline: Supreme Court sets aside High Court order for inquiry into Rahul Gandhi
articles.title: SC sets aside Allahabad HC order on CBI, ED enquiries into disproportionate assets complaint against Rahul Gandhi
articles.summary: The Supreme Court set aside Allahabad High Court orders directing the Central Bureau of Investigation and the Enforcement Directorate to probe a disproportionate assets complaint against Lok Sabha Opposition Leader Rahul Gandhi. A three-judge bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant ruled that Gandhi must be impleaded as a party and heard from the threshold, criticizing the previous in-chamber proceedings.
articles.description: Three-judge bench led by CJI India Surya Kant directs the Opposition leader be impleaded as a party, while relegating the case back to the High Court to be heard from the very threshold in open court by a fresh Bench of judges

articles.headline: Supreme Court clarifies students opting for three languages may continue
articles.title: Students who opted for three languages can continue with them, says Supreme Court
articles.summary: The Supreme Court observed on November 25, 2026, that students currently opting for three languages may continue their choice without mandatory switching. The remarks responded to a Central Board of Secondary Education plea modifying evaluation rules. While Classes 7 through 9 have transitional relaxations, authorities debate implementation schedules and student incentives for learning additional languages.
articles.description: Class 7 students, along with Classes 8 and 9, had been granted a transitional relaxation from the CBSE Board exam in the third language when they reached Class 10

articles.headline: D. Gukesh and Javokhir Sindarov draw second World Chess Championship game
articles.title: World Chess Championship: Gukesh, Sindarov sign peace treaty in quick time
articles.summary: Grandmasters D. Gukesh and Javokhir Sindarov agreed to a draw in the second game of the World Chess Championship in Geneva on Wednesday. Utilizing the London System opening, the twenty-year-old competitors reached a threefold repetition after thirty moves. The result leaves the youngest World title match in history tied at one point each after two rounds.
articles.description: It is all-square in the youngest World title match in history; it is D. Gukesh 1, Javokhir Sindarov 1

articles.headline: Jensen Huang returns as Nvidia chief executive officer
articles.title: Jensen Huang needs a new playbook for his second innings at Nvidia
articles.summary: Co-founder Jensen Huang resumed his role at Nvidia in California on November 23, 2026, following intensive lobbying by tech billionaires. Huang apologized to employees after a scandal-driven exit wiped out a quarter of the company value. His reinstatement immediately boosted market capitalization by nearly a trillion dollars as company stock surged.
articles.description: Returning to Nvidia’s Santa Clara headquarters in California on Monday (November 23, 2026), and standing on the ground floor of the atrium, Jensen Huang apologised to employees and vowed to be a better CEO

articles.headline: Kim Jong Un urges wider deployment of tactical nuclear weapons
articles.title: Kim Jong Un says North Korea should widen deployment of tactical nukes
articles.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un called for expanded deployment of tactical nuclear weapons across multiple domains during an inspection reported by state media KCNA on Thursday. Kim stated that North Korea's nuclear status is inviolable and warned that any denial is an open declaration of war amid ongoing border tensions with South Korea.
articles.description: North Korean leader warns attempts to deny country's nuclear status will be seen as "an open declaration of war".

articles.headline: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva secures record fourth presidential term in Brazil
articles.title: Lula wins a record fourth presidential term as Brazil defeats far-right, defies Trump and Meta
articles.summary: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva secured a historic fourth presidential term in a runoff election on October 26, 2026, defeating Flávio Bolsonaro of the Liberal Party with 64 million votes. Declaring victory in Villavicencio, Mr. Lula pledged to regulate big tech companies and govern for all Brazilians. The result dealt a setback to U.S. President Donald Trump, who had supported Mr. Bolsonaro, according to special presidential advisor Celso Amorim.
articles.description: People went out to vote because we managed to convince them that their votes were extremely important to safeguarding democracy in the country, said Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva

articles.headline: Ukrainian forces strike Russian military base and damage aircraft
articles.title: Ukraine says five jets damaged in attack on Russia’s Savasleyka airbase
articles.summary: Ukrainian forces attacked the Savasleyka airbase in the Nizhny Novgorod region on Wednesday, damaging five aircraft including MiG-31 jets and Su-34 fighter-bombers, according to the Ukrainian General Staff. The long-range strike aims to cripple Moscow military capabilities amid ongoing conflict and severe Russian attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure.
articles.description: The Ukrainian General Staff says its forces struck an airbase in the Nizhny Novgorod region east of Moscow.

articles.headline: IN-SPACe report highlights India's heavy reliance on imported satellite components
articles.title: India’s satellite supply chain ‘highly dependent on imports’, says space body
articles.summary: India's satellite manufacturing supply chain remains highly dependent on imports for critical components, according to an Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre report released on November 25, 2026. Chairman Pawan Goenka noted that electronics and specialized materials account for nearly 60% of costs. The autonomous body emphasized that addressing gaps in testing and procurement could help India become a global space exporter.
articles.description: India’s space economy is currently valued at nearly $9 billion and is set to grow to $40-45 billion in less than a decade

articles.headline: ISIL blamed for multiple suicide attacks in Syria
articles.title: ISIL blamed for multiple suicide attacks in Syria
articles.description: ISIL suicide attack kills two in an assault on a security post in northeastern Syria.

articles.headline: ISIL suicide attack kills two security personnel in Syria
articles.title: Two Syrian security personnel killed in ISIL suicide attack
articles.summary: An ISIL suicide attack killed two security personnel and wounded five others in Hasakah, Syria, after four gunmen targeted an Internal Security Forces checkpoint on Wednesday. All four assailants died during the incident, which local authorities and Deputy Governor Ahmed al-Hilali vowed to investigate thoroughly to ensure regional stability.
articles.description: Syrian forces say the attack in northeastern Syria's city of Hasakah involved four assailants who were all killed.

articles.headline: Al-Qaeda and IS branches adapt strategies and community outreach in Africa and the Middle East
articles.title: Has global jihadism failed, or is it simply changing shape?
articles.summary: Jihadist groups are shifting tactics by engaging in local community outreach, such as aid distribution by al-Shabab in Somalia, and forging alliances closer to home instead of pursuing global attacks. According to reports, this strategic evolution follows significant defeats and the high-profile rise of former militant leaders like Syria's president Ahmed al-Sharaa. Internal debates persist between hardliners and pragmatists regarding compromises.
articles.description: Jihadist groups appear to be focusing on local issues rather than global terror. Does it signify a real change?

articles.headline: Houthi group targets Saudi Arabian ports and capital amid escalating regional strikes
articles.title: Houthis target Saudi Arabia’s Red Sea ports as strikes escalate
articles.summary: Yemen’s Houthi group struck Saudi Arabia’s Jizan port and targeted Riyadh and Jeddah on Wednesday, prompting air defence interceptions, as fighting intensified near Taiz. A Saudi-led coalition reported hundreds of air strikes against the group, while the Houthis claimed numerous attacks on civilian sites across Yemen, raising concerns over the humanitarian impact on the vital Hodeidah port.
articles.description: Explosion reported in Sanaa after Saudi air defenses intercept ballistic missiles targeting Riyadh.

articles.headline: Hong Kong residential complex renovation fire leaves 168 people dead
articles.title: A renovation was meant to improve these Hong Kong homes - it ended in a blaze that killed 168
articles.summary: A fast-moving fire at the Wang Fuk Court apartment complex in Hong Kong resulted in 168 fatalities on November 26, 2025. An independent committee report attributed the tragedy to human errors, disabled fire alarms, and flammable scaffolding materials used during mandatory building renovations. Surviving relatives shared accounts of personal loss and subsequent psychological trauma following the unprecedented disaster.
articles.description: A year after one of Hong Kong's deadliest fires, families left behind are still waiting for justice.

articles.headline: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO following Donald Trump intervention
articles.title: Trump faces backlash after saying he 'convinced' Nvidia to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang
articles.summary: Nvidia reinstated Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang on Monday after a brief resignation prompted by reports of an affair with a woman linked to Chinese intelligence. President Donald Trump stated he convinced the board to reverse the decision. The move sparked sharp market gains and fierce political backlash, with congressional Democrats and Republicans vowing immediate investigations into the chipmaker and national security compliance.
articles.description: Nvidia had come under pressure from President Trump to reappoint Huang, whose comeback helped add $1tn to the company's stock value.

articles.headline: Fuel tanker crash on Cairo highway causes massive fire killing thirty-one
articles.title: Thirty-one killed in massive fire as fuel tanker crashes on Cairo highway
articles.summary: Thirty-one people died and twenty-one others suffered injuries after a fuel tanker crashed and burst into flames on a busy highway in the Warraq neighbourhood of Cairo on Wednesday evening, according to the health ministry. Officials stated the vehicle overturned following a fallen power cable. The regional public prosecutor initiated an investigation into the deadly accident.
articles.description: Another 21 are injured after the tanker reportedly overturns on a busy ring road in the Egyptian capital.

articles.headline: Global tech stocks decline further amid ongoing concerns over artificial intelligence investment
articles.title: US stocks fall further as fears over AI intensify
articles.summary: Major technology firms experienced sharp share price drops on Wednesday, with losses affecting Nvidia, Anthropic, Amazon, and Meta. The downturn reflects persistent investor anxiety regarding the sustainability of artificial intelligence spending and recent political developments in the United States. Despite the market volatility, investment bank Goldman Sachs projects that artificial intelligence spending will surpass one trillion dollars in 2026.
articles.description: All three main US indexes were down in early trading, with the tech-dominated Nasdaq down almost 4%.

articles.headline: Gaza municipalities warn winter rains threaten displaced Palestinian shelter camps
articles.title: Winter rains threaten 1,000 Gaza shelter sites, councils warn
articles.summary: Gaza municipal leaders warned on Wednesday that upcoming winter storms threaten roughly one thousand displacement camps due to damaged drainage systems and missing repair supplies. The Union of Gaza Strip Municipalities stated that recent November rains already flooded about seventy thousand tents. Meanwhile, European Commission representatives urged Israel to permit waiting humanitarian aid trucks carrying tents to enter the enclave.
articles.description: About 200,000 tents need replacing, Gaza’s municipalities say, as the EU urges Israel to reopen all crossings.

articles.headline: COP31 climate talks collapse in Antalya over fossil fuel phase-out standoff
articles.title: COP31 talks fail as EU, others reject any climate deal without language on a fossil fuel phase-out
articles.summary: United Nations climate negotiations in Antalya, Turkiye, concluded without consensus on November 22, 2026, after a record 48-hour overtime due to disagreements over fossil fuel language. The European Union, backed by roughly 130 nations, rejected the cover text for lacking phase-out commitments. Conversely, nations like India and Saudi Arabia supported the text, stressing the need for equitable energy transitions.
articles.description: EU, Panama among about 130 parties that refuse to accept COP President’s consensus cover text, alleges that it “greenwashes” fossil fuels; India, China, Saudi Arabia are on the other side of the divide

articles.headline: Benjamin Netanyahu calls for immediate end to corruption trial
articles.title: Netanyahu says corruption trial ‘must end’ as court suggests dropping case
articles.summary: Caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu demanded the immediate conclusion of his ongoing corruption trial after judges in Jerusalem expressed significant doubt regarding the bribery charges against him. During a court hearing on Wednesday, judges indicated low chances of conviction in Case 4000. Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara stated she would consider the recommendations as political opponents negotiate coalition pacts.
articles.description: The judges' recommendations came as Israel's longest-serving prime minister fights for his political survival.

articles.headline: Israeli judges recommend dropping bribery charges against Benjamin Netanyahu
articles.title: Israeli judges recommend dropping most serious charges against Netanyahu
articles.summary: Judges at the Jerusalem District Court suggested that prosecutors drop bribery charges against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu during a Wednesday hearing. The panel summoned Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara to state that conviction chances are low in the primary case. Netanyahu praised the development as his political rival Gadi Eisenkot attempts to form a new government administration.
articles.description: The Israeli PM says his trial should end after judges said there was little chance of conviction in one of three cases.

articles.title: Dozens killed in Egypt vehicle fire
articles.description: At least 30 have been ⁠killed and ⁠15 injured when a vehicle carrying ‌petroleum products caught fire in Egypt.

articles.description: Donald Trump is targeting China, the European Union and 12 other jurisdictions in a new round of tariffs.

articles.title: Ukrainian laser downs Russian jet-powered drone in world first

articles.headline: US Federal Communications Commission approves SpaceX space data centres
articles.title: US grants SpaceX approval for 1 million space data centres
articles.summary: The United States Federal Communications Commission authorised Elon Musk's SpaceX to deploy a constellation of one million space data centres named Starmind. Agency Chairman Brendan Carr stated the decision on Wednesday marks a historical first to support growing artificial intelligence computing demands. Rival companies have previously criticized the ambitious orbital infrastructure deployment plan.
articles.description: Elon Musk hails FCC's approval of SpaceX's Starmind project as 'a great asset to America and the world.'

articles.headline: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as chief executive following government consultations
articles.title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO after U.S. government input
articles.summary: Nvidia unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive on Monday, November 23, 2026, after board members received assurances from senior United States government officials that he posed no national security risk. The decision followed public backing from President Donald Trump, occurring less than two weeks after the 63-year-old co-founder resigned over an alleged spy scandal involving former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang.
articles.description: U.S. President Donald Trump welcomed the move as a “correct and proper decision”

articles.headline: Trump administration announces new tariffs on fourteen trading partners
articles.title: World reacts to Trump’s new tariffs as US stocks tumble
articles.summary: The United States administration announced new import tariffs targeting fourteen major trading partners, including China and the European Union, citing structural manufacturing overcapacity. The levies follow an investigation led by Trade Representative Jamieson Greer under Section 301. Following the announcement on Wednesday, US stock indices tumbled significantly while bond yields dropped across both America and Europe.
articles.description: The new levies come after an eight-month investigation launched by the United States Trade Representative.

articles.headline: Wall Street rallies sharply as Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as chief executive
articles.title: Wall Street roars back as Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
articles.summary: Main United States stock indexes surged on Monday, November 23, 2026, driven by a record 32.2% jump in Nvidia shares after the chipmaker reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive. The Nasdaq Composite climbed 6.69% to 24,131.42, fueled by widespread gains across artificial intelligence and tech stocks. Investors now await upcoming inflation data from Wednesday's personal consumption expenditures report to gauge Federal Reserve monetary policy.
articles.description: Nvidia shares surged 32.2%, on track for their biggest one-day jump in more than two decades after an extraordinary reversal, which followed President Donald Trump’s call for Jensen Huang’s return

articles.headline: Ukrainian drone strikes hit industrial facilities in Russia's Samara region
articles.title: Ukraine says it struck two oil refineries in Russia's Samara region
articles.summary: Ukrainian drone attacks struck industrial facilities in Syzran and killed one person in Samara on November 25, 2026, according to local authorities. Governor Vyacheslav Fedorishchev reported that air defence downed 145 drones, causing power outages. Unverified social media reports indicated two oil refineries were hit, following Russian President Vladimir Putin's pledge to retaliate for previous strikes.
articles.description: Samara’s regional governor, ​Vyacheslav Fedorishchev, said on social media that local air defence ⁠forces had downed 145 Ukrainian drones overnight, causing power outages

articles.headline: Israeli airstrike in Gaza kills senior Hamas official and family
articles.title: Israeli strike kills Hamas official, his wife and children
articles.summary: An Israeli military airstrike in the Beach refugee camp killed Hamas colonel Mohammad Abuelouf alongside his wife and two children on November 25, 2026, according to medics and Gaza's Interior Ministry. The military stated Abuelouf advanced attacks against Israeli forces in violation of a ceasefire. The attack followed another strike that killed internal security head Naeem Abu Nahel.
articles.description: The Israeli military confirmed it had killed Abuelouf, whom it described as a significant figure who "served as ‌a key source of expertise in efforts to restrict the IDF’s counterterrorism operations in the ‌Gaza ⁠Strip"

articles.headline: FCC authorizes SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million AI satellites
articles.title: FCC signs off on SpaceX’s plan to put up to 1 million data center satellites into space
articles.summary: The Federal Communications Commission approved a plan by Elon Musk-owned SpaceX to launch up to 1 million AI chip-equipped satellites under the Starmind initiative, marking the first agency approval for a full satellite constellation. The decision requires at least one deployment by 2033 and full completion by 2040, though the agency deferred a request regarding graveyard orbits due to insufficient disposal details.
articles.description: In an announcement on Wednesday, the FCC says it authorized SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million AI chip-equipped satellites as part of the Elon Musk-owned company's "Starmind" initiative. With several others also pursuing the idea of putting AI data centers in space, including Google and Blue Origin, this is the first approval the agency […]

articles.headline: Trump’s tariff plan explained: Which countries could be hit and why?
articles.title: Trump’s tariff plan explained: Which countries could be hit and why?
articles.description: The Trump administration is preparing a fresh tariff offensive targeting major trading partners including China, India and the European Union. Here’s what the investigation is about and what it could mean for global trade.

articles.headline: Iraq court rules federal government can take over Kurdish borders and oil fields
articles.title: Iraq’s top court rules government can take over Kurdish borders, oil fields
articles.summary: The Federal Supreme Court in Iraq ruled that federal forces can deploy to international borders in the Kurdish region and oversee oil fields. The decision supports Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi's efforts to curb oil smuggling and centralise state authority. Kurdish authorities condemned the ruling as an assault on constitutional rights, while analysts highlighted potential challenges in implementing these measures against armed factions.
articles.description: The ruling comes a day after Kurdish authorities accused Baghdad of an 'assault' on the region's constitutional rights.

articles.headline: RBI bulletin indicates continued broad-based pressure on food prices in November
articles.title: Broad-based pressure on food prices continues: RBI Bulletin
articles.summary: High-frequency data up to November 19 reveal persistent inflationary pressures on food items across India, according to a Reserve Bank of India report. Prices for cereals, pulses, and edible oils increased, while vegetable prices showed mixed trends. Officials noted that strong credit growth and robust export performance continue to support domestic economic resilience despite challenging global conditions and geopolitical risks.
articles.description: CPI inflation peaked to 6.1 % (y-o-y) in October 2026 from 5.5% in September 2026, slightly above the upper tolerance level of 6%–last observed in October 2024.

articles.headline: Jerusalem Daily: Israel kills Hamas’s Gaza security chief
articles.title: Jerusalem Daily: Israel kills Hamas’s Gaza security chief
articles.description: Israel assassinated Hamas’s internal security chief in Gaza City, killing him and six others in a strike

articles.headline: India records lowest net foreign direct investment in over five years during September
articles.title: Net FDI fell to more than 5.5-year low in September 2026, as outflows jumped 40%
articles.summary: Net foreign direct investment into India dropped to negative 4.95 billion dollars in September 2026, marking the lowest level since at least March 2021. Reserve Bank of India data indicates the decline stemmed from a drop in gross inflows to 5.9 billion dollars alongside a surge in outward investments and profit repatriations by foreign companies totaling 10.8 billion dollars.
articles.description: Despite September’s performance, net FDI in the first half of the financial year was more than 20% higher than in the same period last year

articles.headline: Ukraine reports five Russian military jets damaged in strike on Savasleyka airfield
articles.title: Five Russian military jets hit in airfield strike, says Ukraine
articles.summary: Kyiv's General Staff stated that three MiG-31 and two Su-34 aircraft were damaged during a drone strike on the Savasleyka airfield located 300 kilometres east of Moscow. Russian officials have not commented on the airfield attack, which follows separate overnight strikes on oil refineries in the Samara region that left one person dead, according to regional governor Vyacheslav Fedorishchev.
articles.description: The Savasleyka airfield hosts aircraft used by Russia to launch hypersonic missiles and glide bombs at Ukraine.

articles.headline: Israeli air strike kills senior Hamas security official in Gaza City
articles.title: Israeli strike kills senior Hamas security official and family in Gaza City
articles.summary: An Israeli air strike in the Gaza Strip killed Mohammed Abu al-Ouf, a senior Hamas internal security official, along with three members of his family at dawn. The military described the target as a terrorist. The attack caused extensive damage in Shati refugee camp, drawing strong condemnation from the Hamas-run interior ministry amid ongoing conflict.
articles.description: Mohammed Abu al-Ouf, head of Hamas's internal security service in northern Gaza, was killed with his wife and two teenage daughters, doctors say.

articles.headline: Indian stock indices and rupee surge amid foreign capital inflows
articles.title: Stock indices gain 1.85%, rupee surges to 8-month high aided by foreign inflows, low crude prices
articles.summary: Benchmark equity indices on November 25, 2026, recorded a significant gain of 1.85 percent backed by fresh large-cap buying and easing Brent crude oil prices below $90 a barrel. Simultaneously, the Indian rupee surged to an eight-month high against the dollar, reaching 92.23 in the interbank market. Analysts attributed the positive financial momentum to robust foreign portfolio investor inflows and improved domestic market liquidity.
articles.description: Investors' wealth went up by ₹3.49 lakh crore to ₹5,12,48,042.08 crore (USD 5.54 trillion) on November 25

articles.headline: Bangladesh tightens border security and deploys paramilitary forces
articles.title: Bangladesh tightens border security ahead of Hasina's planned return; deploys 108 BGB platoons
articles.summary: Bangladesh deployed 108 platoons of border paramilitary forces across seven districts to maintain order amid rising political tensions and violence surrounding the planned return of exiled former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina. Authorities increased surveillance and patrols following incidents of arson and clashes linked to the banned Awami League party ahead of December.
articles.description: The heightened security comes amid fears that Ms. Hasina's supporters could intensify violence and sabotage in the coming days. Awami League, whose activities have been banned, is promoting a lockdown programme for November 29 and 30 through online platforms, adding to concerns over a possible escalation of tensions

articles.headline: Solomon Islands signs security treaty with Australia
articles.title: Solomon Islands signs security deal with Australia
articles.summary: The Solomon Islands and Australia signed a security treaty on Wednesday prohibiting foreign military bases on the island nation. Australia will provide 740 million Australian dollars over ten years to support infrastructure and education. The agreement requires the Solomon Islands to consult Canberra on critical infrastructure deals, marking a shift away from recent Chinese influence.
articles.description: Solomon Islands will have to consult Canberra before making new security or infrastructure deals under new pact.

articles.headline: Leaked Russian statistics reveal nearly 500,000 military fatalities
articles.title: Russia's own figures show it has lost nearly 500,000 people in Ukraine war
articles.summary: Leaked official data from Russia's statistics agency Rosstat, analysed by the BBC and independent outlet Mediazona following a cyber-attack, indicates that at least 490,334 Russian soldiers have died since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine began in 2022. The records demonstrate severe casualties among young adults and specific military units, far exceeding figures acknowledged publicly by Moscow while aligning with open-source tracking efforts.
articles.description: Leaked data reveal how the full-scale invasion of Ukraine has fundamentally changed mortality patterns in Russia.

articles.headline: Russian air strikes across Ukraine kill five and damage energy infrastructure
articles.title: Russian strikes on Ukraine kill five, cause power outages in five regions
articles.summary: Russian military strikes across multiple Ukrainian regions killed at least five people, injured dozens, and severely damaged essential energy facilities, according to local authorities. The attacks caused widespread power outages in Dnipropetrovsk, Donetsk, Zaporizhia, Odesa, and Kharkiv. Furthermore, the Russian-occupied Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant temporarily lost external power following shelling, forcing it to switch to diesel generators during the ongoing conflict.
articles.description: A Ukrainian official says attacks on Zaporizhia and Dnipropetrovsk regions damaged a number of energy sites.

articles.headline: Rapid Support Forces drone attacks kill nineteen people in Sudan
articles.title: Sudan’s RSF kills at least 19 in drone attacks on Blue Nile state
articles.summary: At least 19 individuals were killed and 20 others wounded after paramilitary Rapid Support Forces launched overnight drone strikes targeting Damazin, the capital of Sudan's Blue Nile state. A rights group and military sources reported that the bombardment hit residential areas, electricity infrastructure, and a nearby dam. This violence forms part of the ongoing civil war between Sudanese military factions that began in April 2023.
articles.description: The attacks on Blue Nile state also wounded at least 20 people – in a drone war that is quickly escalating.

articles.headline: After Brexit, is Britain heading back to the EU?
articles.title: After Brexit, is Britain heading back to the EU?
articles.description: A decade after the Brexit vote, a new deal brings Britain and the EU closer, with economic gains for both sides.

articles.headline: Israeli air strike kills senior Hamas security official in Gaza
articles.title: Israeli strike in Gaza kills senior Hamas official, his wife and children
articles.summary: An Israeli military air attack in the Gaza Strip killed Muhammad Majid Abu al-Awf, the director of the Internal Security Service in northern Gaza, along with his wife and two daughters. The enclave's Ministry of Interior stated that the strike targeted their residence in the Shati refugee camp. This incident occurred shortly after the killing of another senior security official amid continuing violence in the region.
articles.description: Gaza's internal security director and his family are among seven Palestinians killed by Israeli forces on Wednesday.

articles.headline: Huawei found guilty of trade secrets conspiracy and bank fraud in U.S.
articles.title: Huawei found guilty of stealing US trade secrets but acquitted of racketeering
articles.summary: Following a two-month trial in a Brooklyn court, a United States jury found Chinese technology firm Huawei guilty of ten out of twelve counts, including conspiracy to steal trade secrets and bank fraud. Jurors acquitted the company of an overarching racketeering charge. Defence attorney Brian Heberlig announced that Huawei plans to appeal the convictions following the sentencing scheduled for September 2027.
articles.description: The verdict follows a months-long trial in New York.

articles.headline: Chinese Communist Party investigates Shanghai party secretary Chen Jining
articles.title: Who is Chen Jining, China’s latest Politburo member under investigation?
articles.summary: The Chinese Communist Party launched an anticorruption probe into Shanghai secretary Chen Jining for alleged serious violations of discipline and law. Announced by the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection, the investigation makes Chen the fourth high-ranking Political Bureau member to be ousted in two years. President Xi Jinping's ongoing purge aims to enforce strict party discipline ahead of the upcoming congress.
articles.description: Chen is the fourth high-ranking Politburo member to be pushed out in two years.

articles.headline: Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot attempts to form coalition government
articles.title: Could Netanyahu take Israel into another war with Iran to cling to power?
articles.summary: Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot is working to assemble a coalition government to avert potential political maneuvers by interim Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu regarding Iran. Eisenkot currently lacks a majority in the 120-seat Knesset. Intelligence officials and analysts dispute claims of an imminent military threat from Tehran, suggesting any new conflict could be politically motivated to delay ongoing leadership negotiations.
articles.description: As Israeli opposition leader Eisenkot moves to form a government, could war with Iran derail talks and save Netanyahu?

articles.headline: Leaked documents reveal FIFA considered 96-year private equity deal
articles.title: Leaked FIFA documents show Infantino’s 96-year private equity plan for World Cup
articles.summary: Leaked documents reviewed by The Associated Press show FIFA president Gianni Infantino planned to sell stakes in the World Cup for 96 years through a for-profit subsidiary named FIFA Forward Enterprises. The secretive project, developed with Joshua Kushner's firm Thrive Capital, collapsed following a global backlash. Infantino now faces his first presidential election challenge ahead of a March vote in Morocco.
articles.description: The leaked documents, including a FIFA in-house risk assessment, show its own finance officials “were not directly privy to the construction of this transaction”

articles.headline: Trump administration prepares new tariffs following excess industrial capacity probe
articles.title: U.S. set to slap tariffs on China, EU and others after probe on excess industrial capacity: report
articles.summary: The United States administration is set to release findings from a Section 301 investigation concerning excess industrial capacity across sixteen trading partners, with new import duties expected. According to sources, the proposed levies will stack on previous tariffs and replace measures struck down by the Supreme Court in February. The probe covers major economies including the European Union, China, and India.
articles.description: India was also named among 16 ⁠major U.S. trading partners; Together, the duties are meant to ​rebuild Trump’s global “Liberation Day” tariffs that were struck down by the U.S. Supreme Court in February

articles.headline: COP31 climate conference concludes in Antalya without a cover decision
articles.title: COP31 and the unmet promises of climate action
articles.summary: The 31st Conference of the Parties in Antalya, Türkiye, ended two days behind schedule without reaching a final cover decision due to disagreements over naming fossil fuels. The summit highlighted an ongoing inability to operationalize previous commitments from Baku and Belém. According to the Global Carbon Budget 2025, current emission trajectories risk exhausting the carbon budget for 1.5 degrees celsius warming within four years.
articles.description: COP31 has once again laid out the gap between what countries promise and what they are actually prepared to do. With the window to keep warming below 1.5 degrees rapidly closing, the coming year should be spent on fixing what is broken

articles.headline: Flipkart chief executive Kalyan Krishnamurthy to step down
articles.title: Kalyan Krishnamurthy to step down as Flipkart CEO
articles.summary: Flipkart announced that Chief Executive Officer Kalyan Krishnamurthy will step down after more than eleven years with the Bengaluru-based e-commerce firm.
