articles.headline: Australian Parliament passes Digital Duty of Care legislation for tech firms
articles.title: Australia’s Digital Duty of Care law: Why Big Tech is under pressure
articles.summary: The Australian Parliament enacted the Digital Duty of Care Bill on November 25, 2026, legally obligating online services, social media platforms, games, apps, and artificial intelligence chatbots to protect users. Companies violating the new regulations face financial penalties reaching up to five percent of their global turnover or 109.2 million Australian dollars. The legislation amends the Online Safety Act 2021 by replacing previous safety codes with a single enforceable duty of care.
articles.description: The law places a legal duty on online services to protect users from serious harm; but the conservative opposition and the United States say the law could lead to censorship of lawful speech

articles.headline: Samajwadi Party leader predicts social polarisation in Uttar Pradesh elections
articles.title: Social polarisation will replace communal polarisation in UP: Ramji Lal Suman
articles.summary: Samajwadi Party leader Ramji Lal Suman stated that the upcoming Uttar Pradesh state election will feature social polarisation instead of traditional communal divisions. Speaking on November 26, 2026, the Rajya Sabha member highlighted strategies for Dalit and Other Backward Classes unity, addressed the party's upcoming manifesto releases, and criticized the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party's governance. He also discussed regional electoral alliances and outreach efforts directed at marginalised communities.
articles.description: Rajya Sabha MP and National General Secretary of the Samajwadi Party said the BJP stood exposed and the marginalised will no longer become the foot soldiers of Hindutva. With the public mood in favour of progressive forces, he advised the Congress to adopt a practical approach in seat-sharing negotiations

articles.headline: Cost of living exceeds minimum wages in three Karnataka cities, study reveals
articles.title: Study finds cost of living way higher than minimum wage in Bengaluru, Mysuru and Mangaluru
articles.summary: An academic study by Kolkata-based forum Fact or Value reveals that the monthly cost of living in Bengaluru, Mangaluru, and Mysuru significantly exceeds statutory minimum wages, leaving most employed residents earning below basic needs. Released on November 24, 2026, the report relies on formulas from the 15th Indian Labour Conference, Supreme Court precedents, and government data. The findings highlight income gaps amid stalled wage revisions in Karnataka.
articles.description: While the monthly cost of living is calculated to be ₹41,752 in Bengaluru, between 59.9% and 74.6% of employed residents earn less, exposing the stark income gap

articles.headline: Jharkhand Chief Minister moves resolution against amended Mines and Minerals Act
articles.title: Jharkhand CM moves resolution against amended Mines and Minerals Act, claims ₹13,000 crore annual revenue loss
articles.summary: Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren moved a resolution during the special Assembly session on November 26, 2026, seeking the withdrawal of the amended Mines and Minerals Act. According to Mr. Soren, the legislation passed by Parliament in August will cause an annual revenue loss of approximately ₹13,000 crore, significantly impacting public welfare funding.
articles.description: Moving the resolution, Hemant Soren said the amendment, passed by Parliament in August, would adversely affect the State's financial position and its ability to fund welfare and development programmes

articles.headline: European football clubs face mixed results in Champions League matches
articles.title: Champions League: Man United and PSG held to draws, Bayern loses
articles.summary: Manchester United and Paris Saint-Germain were both held to 2-2 draws by Sporting Lisbon and Roma respectively on November 26, 2026, while Bayern Munich suffered a 2-1 defeat against Lille. In other matches, Barcelona secured a 4-1 victory over Sabah, Liverpool defeated Club Brugge 3-0, Atletico Madrid beat Viking 2-0, and Inter Milan overcame Stuttgart 2-0.
articles.description: Barcelona and Liverpool register big wins; Real Madrid tops table

articles.headline: Ukraine targets Russian vessels in Libyan waters amid widening conflict escalation
articles.title: Is Libya a new front in the Ukraine war?
articles.summary: Ukrainian forces claimed responsibility for attacking two Russian vessels in Libyan waters, destroying a warship in Benghazi and striking an offshore cargo vessel. The escalation threatens to draw the politically divided North African nation into the ongoing conflict. Defence analysts and officials discussed the strategic implications of these rare overseas strikes on Russian naval assets.
articles.description: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says two Russian vessels were targeted in Libya's waters.

articles.headline: Jannik Sinner ruled out of 2027 Australian Open following knee surgery
articles.title: Jannik Sinner ruled out of 2027 Australian Open after knee surgery
articles.summary: World number two Jannik Sinner will miss the Australian Open in January 2027 as he recovers from right knee surgery performed in Finland. According to Tennis Australia chief Andrew Abdo, the Italian player aims to return for the 2028 tournament, leaving Alexander Zverev to take over the top ranking during his absence.
articles.description: Sinner, a two-time champion at Melbourne Park, has not played a match since winning the 2026 Wimbledon title in July.

articles.headline: Senior Hamas security official killed in Israeli drone strikes
articles.title: Senior Hamas security official killed in Israeli drone strikes
articles.description: A senior Hamas security official has been killed in a series of Israeli strikes across Gaza

articles.headline: Sri Lankan mass grave revives search for justice regarding Muslim massacres
articles.title: Sri Lanka mass grave revives quest for answers to forgotten Muslim massacre
articles.summary: The discovery of skeletal remains in a Kurukkalmadam mass grave has renewed efforts by families to identify victims and secure dignified burials for relatives killed during Sri Lanka's civil war. The conflict saw significant violence against the Muslim population by Tamil rebels in the early 1990s, including massacres and forced expulsions.
articles.description: As Sri Lanka's Tamil separatists fought a deadly war with the army, they also killed hundreds of Muslims.

articles.headline: Bank of Korea raises key interest rate and upgrades growth forecast
articles.title: South Korea’s central bank hikes interest rates amid AI chip boom
articles.summary: The Bank of Korea increased its benchmark interest rate by 0.25 percentage points to 3.25 percent on November 26, 2026, driven by robust domestic growth and high inflation. Citing strong artificial intelligence investments and soaring semiconductor exports, the central bank also upgraded its gross domestic product growth forecasts to 3.9 percent for 2026 and 4.1 percent for 2027.
articles.description: Bank of Korea raises key rate by 0.25 percent amid booming exports of semiconductors.

articles.headline: Leaders pay tribute to victims and security personnel on Mumbai attack anniversary
articles.title: 2008 Mumbai terror attacks: Tributes paid to martyrs on 18th anniversary
articles.summary: Political leaders and senior officials gathered at the Mumbai police headquarters on November 26, 2026, to honor victims and security personnel killed during the 2008 terror attacks. The coordinated strikes, executed by ten Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorists arriving by sea from Pakistan, resulted in 166 fatalities and over 300 injuries across multiple iconic locations over three days.
articles.description: Ten LeT terrorists from Pakistan arrived by sea on November 26, 2008, and killed 166 people, including 18 security personnel, during a 60-hour siege of Mumbai

articles.headline: European spacecraft captures images of stadium-sized crater on asteroid Dimorphos
articles.title: New images reveal crater on asteroid hit by NASA’s DART planetary defence mission
articles.summary: New images released by the European Space Agency reveal a stadium-sized impact crater and chaotic tumbling on the asteroid Dimorphos following its collision with NASA's DART spacecraft in September 2022. The Hera spacecraft captured the close-up views from a distance to evaluate how the kinetic impactor technique altered the celestial body's trajectory for planetary defense.
articles.description: The DART, short for Double Asteroid Redirection ⁠Test, spacecraft collided with Dimorphos on September 26, 2022; asteroid tumbles in space, with boulders flying around

articles.headline: India plans open-entry caste question for upcoming 2027 national census
articles.title: How should the Census count caste?
articles.summary: India's 2027 census will incorporate an open-entry caste question for populations outside Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, a method previously utilized during the 2011 socio-economic survey. While critics warn of reconciliation challenges arising from millions of distinct entries, officials plan to utilize code directories to process responses following the enumeration beginning in February 2027.
articles.description: The 2027 Census will enumerate caste through an open-entry question, risking a repeat of the 2011 Socio-Economic and Caste Census, which returned about 46.7 lakh caste names; recording the administrative category alongside the caste name would give India reliable caste-wise information on education, occupation and assets

articles.headline: Cameroon separatist leader Lucas Cho Ayaba pleads not guilty in Norway
articles.title: Cameroon separatist leader pleads not guilty at war crimes trial in Norway
articles.summary: Cameroonian separatist leader Lucas Cho Ayaba pleaded not guilty in an Oslo court on Tuesday to terrorism and war crimes charges carrying a sentence of up to thirty years. Prosecutors accuse the fifty-four-year-old of remotely directing attacks, including a two thousand twenty-three blast in Buea that killed a woman and a two thousand twenty-four explosion in Nkambe that killed a teenager. The trial is scheduled to run until March twelve.
articles.description: Lucas Cho Ayaba is accused of remotely planning attacks that killed and injured dozens of civilians.

articles.headline: Russian attack in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia kills two people and injures 22
articles.title: A Russian strike on Ukraine kills two, wounds 48 as Kyiv explains its attack in Libya
articles.summary: A Russian attack on Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia killed two people and injured 22 others, including two children. Ivan Fedorov, co-head of the Zaporizhzhia Regional Defense Council, reported the overnight strike on Telegram. Regional Governor Mykhailo Semikin stated people might be trapped under rubble after apartments and infrastructure were damaged. Russia's Defence Ministry reported separate strikes in the Sumy region.
articles.description: A Russian nighttime attack on Zaporizhzhia in southern Ukraine has killed two civilians and wounded 48 others including four children

articles.headline: Puerto Rico Supreme Court cancels government contract with Luma Energy
articles.title: Puerto Rico’s Supreme Court cancels major power contract
articles.summary: Puerto Rico Supreme Court ruled in favour of ending the government contract with Luma Energy following a lawsuit by San Juan. The five-to-four decision on Wednesday outlines a one-year transition period. Governor Jenniffer Gonzalez blamed Luma for constant interruptions and record electricity costs, while a federal control board warned the ruling creates enormous uncertainty without a clear successor company in place.
articles.description: The court's five-to-four ruling ends Luma Energy's operations after a contentious legal battle.

articles.headline: Indian rupee falls twenty paise against United States dollar
articles.title: Rupee falls 20 paise to 92.40 against U.S. dollar in early trade
articles.summary: The Indian rupee depreciated twenty paise to 92.40 against the United States dollar on November 26, 2026. Forex traders stated that higher crude oil prices and United States tariff proposals against India fuelled dollar demand. The United States proposed twenty-five percent tariffs following an investigation, while India rejected the allegation and expressed commitment to a bilateral trade agreement.
articles.description: The U.S. proposed 25% tariffs on imports from India, with a provision to cap them at 17% if the two countries agree to a bilateral trade deal, giving it a slight edge over Asian competitors

articles.headline: After Libya, where will Ukraine strike Russia next?
articles.title: After Libya, where will Ukraine strike Russia next?
articles.description: From Libya to Sudan and Mali, Ukraine is targeting Russia's military networks across Africa.

articles.headline: Artificial intelligence models achieve breakthroughs on longstanding mathematical problems in 2026
articles.title: Top 10 math problems AI models have taken a run at in 2026 (so far)
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence models have achieved significant milestones by tackling major unresolved mathematical problems throughout 2026. On November 25, OpenAI announced that an internal model established the theoretical speed limit for matrix multiplication, following a July 20 achievement where mathematician Levent Alpöge used Anthropic's Claude model to disprove the Jacobian conjecture. While many experts celebrate these technological advancements, others express concern regarding methodological transparency and education.
articles.description: A flurry of announcements landed in the third week of November claiming that various artificial intelligence (AI) models had solved longstanding mathematical problems

articles.headline: German boat dealer suspected of supplying migrant smuggling networks
articles.title: Watch: BBC confronts German man suspected of supplying migrant gangs with small boats
articles.summary: A German boat dealer is suspected by European authorities of supplying small boats and engines to migrant smuggling gangs operating in the English Channel. According to documents seen by the BBC, equipment from MaReBoote was linked to nearly a third of small-boat crossings to the United Kingdom in early 2026. Managing director Marvin Reuter is currently contesting extradition to France to face charges.
articles.description: Marvin Reuter is contesting extradition to France, where he could face smuggling, criminal conspiracy and involuntary manslaughter charges.

articles.headline: German boat dealer investigated over English Channel migrant smuggling
articles.title: German boat dealer suspected of supplying Channel smuggling gangs, BBC finds
articles.summary: European authorities are investigating a German boat dealer accused of supplying vessels and engines to migrant smuggling networks operating in the English Channel. Marvin Reuter, managing director of MaReBoote, is contesting extradition to France after being linked to numerous illegal crossings and two fatal accidents. French prosecutor Samuel Finielz confirmed a European Arrest Warrant was issued for the German company head in May 2025.
articles.description: Nearly a third of crossings in early 2026 allegedly involved boats or engines from the German man's firm.

articles.headline: Six people killed in small plane crash off Mississippi
articles.title: Six killed, including children, in plane crash off Mississippi coast
articles.summary: First responders recovered the bodies of six members from two families after a small plane crashed in the Gulf of Mexico off the Mississippi coast on Tuesday. The Cessna 210 was travelling from New Orleans to Fort Myers when air traffic control lost contact at about 3:45 pm. Authorities are investigating the cause, including potential weather impacts like dangerous icing conditions.
articles.description: US authorities are investigating the reason behind the crash that killed members of the Stokes and Knox families.

articles.headline: Yashasvi Jaiswal emerges as a reliable opening batter for the Indian Test team
articles.title: Jaiswal — the all-terrain red-ball machine
articles.summary: Following India's transition after the World Test Championship final in June 2023, left-handed batsman Yashasvi Jaiswal secured his place as a Test opener. Making his debut in Roseau on July 12, 2023, he scored 171 runs and subsequently demonstrated notable adaptability across diverse pitch conditions in the Caribbean, South Africa, and home series against England, establishing himself as a prolific run-scorer for the national side.
articles.description: The four away Tests right at the start of his career were a great learning experience for him. After his debut in the Caribbean where the pitches played low and slow, those in South Africa were of the exactly opposite kind and opened the young man’s eyes to the challenges that would confront him in the longest format

articles.headline: Sheikh Hasina announces plans to return to Bangladesh from exile
articles.title: Hasina to return to Bangladesh on December 16, says Awami League
articles.summary: Ousted former Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina stated her intention to travel back to her home country from India on December 16. The planned date coincides with Victory Day, marking the nation's independence following a war with Pakistan. Ms. Hasina departed her position on August 5, 2024, after massive protests ended her tenure, and she has now urged current leadership to facilitate her air transport.
articles.description: Ousted Prime Minister has asked Bangladesh government for an aircraft; Awami League team has visited Petrapole in West Bengal to assess Benapole-Petrapole crossing in case Ms. Hasina plans to enter Bangladesh trough land border crossing

articles.headline: Madras High Court issues John Doe order regarding Thirupparankundram hill lamp lighting
articles.title: Thirupparankundram Deepathoon row: What does John Doe order passed by Madras HC mean?
articles.summary: The Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court issued a John Doe order restraining the public from violating a Supreme Court ruling on lighting a ceremonial lamp at Thirupparankundram hill. The Supreme Court previously permitted the event as a limited arrangement, despite ongoing ownership disputes between Hindu worshippers and a local dargah regarding the site's hilltop location.
articles.description: The Madras High Court restrained anyone from violating the November 20 Supreme Court order which allowed the lighting of the lamp on the hillock as a ‘limited one-time arrangement’ only.

articles.headline: BJP, Akali Dal reunite ahead of Punjab polls as Sukhbir Badal brings SAD back to NDA
articles.title: BJP, Akali Dal reunite ahead of Punjab polls as Sukhbir Badal brings SAD back to NDA
articles.description: In a major political development ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections, the Shiromani Akali Dal has formally returned to the National Democratic Alliance (NDA), ending a six-year separation from the BJP.

articles.headline: Jannik Sinner withdraws from the 2027 Australian Open due to knee surgery
articles.title: Jannik Sinner out of Australian Open 2027 due to knee injury
articles.summary: Italian tennis player Jannik Sinner will miss the 2027 Australian Open while recovering from recent right knee surgery. Tennis Australia chief executive Andrew Abdo confirmed on November 26, 2026, that the defending champion will be absent from the tournament beginning January 17 in Melbourne. Sinner previously underwent a minor operation on November 24 following persistent joint inflammation that failed to respond to prior treatments.
articles.description: “Jannik loves competing here in Melbourne and is looking forward to returning for AO 2028. We wish him all the very best with his recovery and look forward to seeing him back on court soon”

articles.headline: Karnataka approves India's first comprehensive care and rehabilitation policy for burns survivors
articles.title: Karnataka charts India’s first comprehensive care and rehabilitation policy for burns survivors
articles.summary: The Karnataka Cabinet has approved a policy for the prevention, treatment, rehabilitation, and social reintegration of burns survivors, making it the first state in India to implement such a framework. The initiative involves establishing 15-bed burns care wards in district and medical college hospitals while upgrading the Mahabodhi Burns Care Centre at the Bangalore Medical College and Research Institute into a Centre of Excellence to address statewide treatment gaps.
articles.description: 15-bed burns care wards to be set up in district hospitals; Bangalore Medical College and Research Institute’s Mahabodhi Burns Care Centre to be upgraded as Centre of Excellence

articles.headline: Macy’s postpones its centenary Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York due to severe weather
articles.title: Macy's postpones Thanksgiving parade due to severe weather
articles.summary: Macy’s postponed its 100th annual Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York to Saturday due to an approaching nor'easter storm expected to bring high winds and heavy rain. Executive producer Will Cross said balloons would be deflated for safety, while New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani confirmed increased security for the rescheduled procession amidst regional state of emergency declarations.
articles.description: The move represents the first postponement of the iconic event, and comes after a forecast of strong winds and heavy rain.

articles.headline: Global UN report reveals intentional killings of women by family members
articles.title: Five women killed every hour globally by partner, relative last year: UN
articles.summary: New data released by the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime and UN Women indicates that approximately 47,000 women and girls were killed globally by intimate partners or relatives last year. Published on Tuesday, the report states that Africa recorded the highest victimization rate, while officials emphasized that institutional failures and harmful societal norms continue to endanger female safety worldwide.
articles.description: Home remains the most dangerous place for a woman or girl, 'a pattern that has barely shifted in years', UN Women says.

articles.headline: Prakash Ambedkar warns of potential blood revolution if the Constitution is not protected
articles.title: Country could face a ‘blood revolution’ unless the Constitution is saved: Prakash Ambedkar
articles.summary: Vanchit Bahujan Aghadi chief Prakash Ambedkar warned on November 25, 2026, that India faces a potential blood revolution unless the Constitution is safeguarded. Speaking at the Samvidhan Samman Sabha, Ambedkar alleged that the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party and Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh are threatening democratic ideals through communal politics and by exacerbating regional divides between northern and southern states. He also criticized major opposition figures and raised concerns regarding national security.
articles.description: Prakash Ambedkar said it is “unfortunate” that the ideals of the Constitution were under threat as Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) and the BJP is doing everything to be in power

articles.headline: Israeli air strikes in Gaza kill Hamas internal security chief
articles.title: Israeli air strike kills Hamas internal security chief in Gaza
articles.summary: At least seven people were killed in Israeli air strikes across the Gaza Strip, including Naeem Abu Nahel, the head of Hamas's internal security service. Israeli leaders confirmed the killing in western Gaza City, while separate attacks claimed the lives of six others in Wadi Gaza and Khan Younis. Meanwhile, health authorities warned of rising infection rates amid ongoing humanitarian challenges.
articles.description: Naeem Abu Nahel, who had been in the post for two months, is among seven Palestinians reportedly killed in Israeli strikes on Tuesday.

articles.headline: India pavilion wins Visitors’ Lion at Venice Biennale
articles.title: India Pavilion bags Visitors’ Lion at Venice Biennale; PM Modi calls it ‘proud moment for country’
articles.summary: The India Pavilion won the Visitors’ Lion for Best National Participation at the 61st International Art Exhibition of the Venice Art Biennale, running from May 9 to November 22. Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Culture Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat celebrated the achievement, which highlights the nation's growing cultural influence and showcases works by five artists at the historic Arsenale venue.
articles.description: The pavilion, under the theme ‘Geographies of Distance: Remembering Home’, explored memory and belonging in a rapidly transforming world

articles.headline: China investigates Shanghai party chief Chen Jining for corruption
articles.title: China’s probes Shanghai party chief Chen Jining over corruption
articles.summary: China's anticorruption watchdog has launched a formal investigation into Shanghai party chief Chen Jining for severe violations of discipline and laws. The 62-year-old Politburo member becomes the fourth top-tier leader probed under President Xi Jinping's sweeping campaign. State media reported the inquiry alongside a separate investigation into science ministry official Liu Min.
articles.description: Chen is the fourth Politburo member to be probed since last year in a campaign that has targeted top Chinese leaders.

articles.headline: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei denies supporting AI control over humanity
articles.title: Anthropic CEO Amodei denies wanting humanity to ‘surrender’ free will to AI
articles.summary: Anthropic Chief Executive Officer Dario Amodei addressed reports regarding artificial intelligence governance in a post on X, stating he does not support surrendering human free will to autonomous systems. Responding to an Axios article, Amodei clarified that delegating specific tasks to technology differs from granting global governance authority, as industry leaders continue to debate the timeline and risks surrounding artificial general intelligence.
articles.description: Dario Amodei's remarks come amid predictions AI could soon surpass human intelligence.

articles.headline: Prime Minister Modi highlights constitutional achievements on Constitution Day
articles.title: Govt.’s endeavour has been to deepen Constitution’s connect with people, strengthen unity: PM Modi
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi observed Constitution Day on November 26, 2026, by emphasizing the founding text's role in advancing social and economic justice across the nation. In an op-ed, he detailed welfare initiatives that lifted millions out of poverty, constitutional amendments involving goods and services tax and reservations, and past challenges including the Emergency and Jammu and Kashmir's special status.
articles.description: He pays tribute to Dr. Rajendra Prasad, Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar and all members of the Constituent Assembly, which adopted the Constitution on November 26, 1949; highlights the founding principles’ role in strengthening democracy and promoting social and economic justice

articles.headline: Union Minister Pralhad Joshi announces selected applicants for Kashi Tamil Sangamam
articles.title: 1,400 of 46,080 applicants selected to attend Kashi Tamil Sangamam: Education Minister
articles.summary: Union Minister of Education Pralhad Joshi announced on Tuesday that fourteen hundred applicants out of forty-six thousand eighty were selected for the fifth Kashi Tamil Sangamam running from November 28 to December 12, 2026. Participants will travel to Varanasi in seven groups. The edition introduces a nationwide student programme studying the Thirukkural literary work by poet Thiruvalluvar.
articles.description: The fifth edition of the Kashi Tamil Sangamam features the launch of a nationwide student engagement programme focused on learning the Thirukkural

articles.headline: Petitioners accuse Tamil Nadu government of defying Supreme Court temple lighting order
articles.title: Thirupparankundram row: Supreme Court to examine if wilful disobedience occurred, as State and Hindu parties spar
articles.summary: Petitioners accused the Tamil Nadu government of defying a Supreme Court order regarding the ceremonial lighting of the Karthigai Deepam lamp in Madurai. During a hearing before Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M. Pancholi on November 25, 2026, senior advocate Guru Krishnakumar alleged that the State circumvented the directive by lighting the festival lamp at an alternative customary location instead of the disputed hilltop stone pillar.
articles.description: Madurai Collector claims all arrangements made to light the lamp on the Deepathoon, as per the SC’s November 20 order, but temple did not send team; temple cites ‘historical continuity’; Hindu parties accuse State, temple of collusion to defy order

articles.headline: US military faces mounting infrastructure costs and vulnerabilities in Middle East
articles.title: How the Iran war is reshaping the US military presence in the Middle East
articles.summary: The ongoing conflict with Iran has exposed vulnerabilities across United States military installations in the Middle East, causing billions in infrastructure damage. Repair costs are estimated at $9.4 billion following numerous attacks since February 28, prompting experts to predict potential future reductions and relocations of regional forces once hostilities conclude.
articles.description: Experts say fallout from the war and domestic opposition could force a smaller permanent presence in the Middle East.

articles.headline: Chen Jining placed under disciplinary investigation for suspected severe violations
articles.title: China announces shock corruption probe into Politburo member
articles.summary: Chen Jining, a member of the ruling Communist Party of China Politburo and party leader in Shanghai, was placed under a disciplinary investigation on November 24, 2026. The unexpected inquiry by anti-corruption bodies stunned observers given his high political standing. Chen previously served as Beijing mayor and was widely viewed as a candidate for higher national leadership.
articles.description: Shanghai Party Secretary Chen Jining was earlier expected to assume a top leadership role in 2027

articles.headline: India separates Sheikh Hasina return plans from extradition requests
articles.title: MEA separates Sheikh Hasina’s plans to return to Bangladesh from issue of extradition
articles.summary: The Indian Ministry of External Affairs stated on November 25, 2026, that former Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina returning home voluntarily using a travel document is separate from Bangladesh's formal extradition request. Official spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal also expressed deep concern regarding ongoing violence against minorities in Bangladesh during the press briefing.
articles.description: ‘The case of a citizen willing to return voluntarily to her country on a travel document is a matter separate from the extradition request,’ MEA’s official spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said

articles.headline: Vladimir Putin warns West over Kaliningrad amid rising military tensions in Baltic Sea
articles.title: Kaliningrad: Why Russia’s Baltic exclave is a new flashpoint
articles.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin warned Western nations on October 1, 2026, that Russia would deploy all available weapons if directly attacked over the exclave of Kaliningrad. Moscow accused North Atlantic Treaty Organization countries of increasing military pressure around the territory through heightened activities in the Baltic Sea. NATO rejected the accusations, describing its operations as strictly defensive and denouncing nuclear rhetoric.
articles.description: Moscow has accused the alliance of increasing military pressure around the strategic exclave and has sent a formal diplomatic note to the NATO over what it sees as attempts to isolate the territory; however, NATO has rejected the accusations, saying its activities in the region are ‘defensive’

articles.headline: Houthi drone strike on Riyadh financial district injures eleven people
articles.title: 11 injured in Houthi attack on Riyadh tower, Saudi civil defence says
articles.summary: Eleven individuals sustained injuries following a Houthi attack targeting a prominent tower in Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District on Tuesday. The casualties included citizens from Saudi Arabia, India, Nepal, and Egypt, according to a civil defence spokesperson. Regional leaders strongly condemned the strike, which marked the second attack on the capital's financial hub within a week.
articles.description: Two Saudi nationals, nine foreigners injured in Houthi attack on building in Riyadh's financial district.

articles.headline: NATO military commander warns Russia against attacking alliance territory
articles.title: Estonia on the edge as Russia-NATO tensions rise
articles.summary: General Alexus Grynkewich issued a stark warning on October 12, stating that North Atlantic Treaty Organization forces would destroy anything involved in an attack. The warning highlights escalating tensions along the European border involving Estonia. Established in 1949 to counter Soviet power, the alliance expanded eastward following the 1991 Soviet collapse, setting the stage for renewed regional friction after the 2014 Crimea annexation and 2022 Ukraine invasion.
articles.description: The NATO member is overhauling its military strategy, moving troops closer to the border and investing in long-range arms as Russia is carrying out grey-zone tactics in NATO’s eastern flank; the country’s defence spending is set to rise by 42% in 2026, reaching €2.4 billion, or around 5.4% of its GDP; the U.K. has maintained some 1,200 troops in Estonia as part of NATO’s forward defence

articles.headline: Brazil steps up efforts to regulate Big Tech over election interference
articles.title: Brazil turns heat on Big Tech and Bolsonaro camp over foreign interference in elections
articles.summary: Following President Lula da Silva securing his election victory, the Brazilian government intensified efforts on November 14, 2026, to advance a legislative bill granting the competition regulator CADE enhanced oversight over major technology operations. The proposed measure draws inspiration from European Union regulations and aims to address digital platform interference during the recent electoral campaign, despite encountering strong political resistance from conservative allies of former leader Flávio Bolsonaro.
articles.description: The move follows Lula’s pledge to make digital regulation a priority of his government

articles.headline: Paraguayan President Santiago Pena resigns amid violent banking protests
articles.title: After Donald Trump’s midterm poll rout, South America breathes easy as far-right feels the heat
articles.summary: Hundreds of thousands protested in Asuncion on November 4, 2026, following the locking of accounts in the largest bank, prompting President Santiago Pena to resign. Congress initiated impeachment proceedings, and Senator Antonio Velazquez stated that Pena fled to Argentina without notice. The political upheaval occurred shortly after United States midterm elections altered regional dynamics for conservative leaders, according to diplomatic sources.
articles.description: Just a day after a blue wave swept across the U.S. in midterms election shaking President Donald Trump’s administration, the fall of Santiago Pena carries significance beyond the borders of the country of seven million people

articles.headline: Plane crash off Mississippi coast kills six members of a Florida family
articles.title: Plane crash off coast of Mississippi kills extended family of six on fishing trip
articles.summary: A small aircraft carrying six members of an extended Florida family crashed into the Gulf of Mexico on November 24, 2026, while returning from a fishing trip. Authorities including the Coast Guard confirmed that divers located the victims inside the fuselage of the Cessna 210. The Federal Aviation Administration and the National Transportation Safety Board are investigating the incident.
articles.description: Shortly before losing contact with the plane, an air traffic controller at Gulfport–Biloxi International Airport advised the pilot of precipitation and adverse weather in the area

articles.headline: Israeli air strike kills senior Hamas security official in Gaza
articles.title: Israeli air strike kills senior Hamas security official in Gaza
articles.description: Naim Abu Nahl, 50, was killed in a crowded area while four others, including a Palestinian woman, were wounded.

articles.headline: Flávio Bolsonaro edges out Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in Brazil vote
articles.title: Brazil lurches to the right as Lula falters in the first round of presidential election
articles.summary: Challenger Flávio Bolsonaro led incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva by about 1.8 percentage points in the first round of the presidential election on October 5, 2026. Because neither candidate secured 50 percent, a runoff is scheduled for October 25. Meanwhile, the Liberal Party made historic gains in Congress and the Senate, reflecting a broad rightward shift that expanded by absorbing traditional conservative and centre-right political spaces across Brazil.
articles.description: Instead of winning in the first round, as his supporters had expected, Lula trailed his challenger Flávio Bolsonaro by about 1.8 percentage points, or 2.2 million votes

articles.headline: Brazil files petitions to investigate alleged United States electoral interference
articles.title: Lula draws the line amid Trump interference in Brazil’s close and tough election
articles.summary: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's campaign requested the Federal Supreme Court investigate potential United States electoral interference on September 23, 2026. The Workers' Party also targeted rival Flávio Bolsonaro over alleged foreign support. The petitions followed a United States-led security pact designating two Brazilian criminal groups as shared threats, prompting strong pushback from Brazilian leadership regarding national sovereignty and protection responsibilities.
articles.description: Lula says ‘Brazil does not fit in anyone’s backyard’ even as the country’s top intelligence agency raises the risk of U.S. interference in the October 4 elections to a ‘critical level’. In recent months, the Trump administration has put enormous pressure on Brazil through tariffs and sanctions

articles.headline: John Wright recalls discovering Jasprit Bumrah during a 2013 domestic match
articles.title: How John Wright spotted Jasprit Bumrah
articles.summary: Former India head coach John Wright recounted how he first noticed fast bowler Jasprit Bumrah during a March 2013 match between Mumbai and Gujarat in Ahmedabad. Working as part of the Mumbai Indians support staff, Wright was drawn to the young bowler's consistent delivery of high-pace yorkers. The chance encounter has since drawn renewed attention following a viral photograph of the pair meeting in Lincoln.
articles.description: ‘I watched him bowl an over; they were all yorkers; he tried to bowl everything as yorkers; and he had a bit of pace,’ John Wright reminisced about Jasprit Bumrah

articles.headline: Macy's postpones 100th Thanksgiving Day Parade to Saturday due to severe weather
articles.title: Bad weather postpones Macy’s 100th Thanksgiving Day Parade for first time ever
articles.summary: Organizers announced that Macy's 100th Thanksgiving Day Parade will be postponed from November 26 to November 28, 2026, due to severe weather bringing intense winds and rain to New York City. Mayor Zohran Mamdani supported the decision, noting potential hazards from high winds that could endanger spectators and oversized balloons. This marks the first time in the event's history that it has been rescheduled.
articles.description: The postponement came as New York City is set to get slammed by a storm bringing intense winds and rain to the region

articles.headline: ICE officers smash car window, pepper spray bystanders
articles.title: ICE officers smash car window, pepper spray bystanders
articles.description: Masked ICE agents smashed a car window and forcibly opened its door to arrest a man in California.

articles.headline: California coastal areas face severe flooding threats as king tides peak
articles.title: California warns of flooding as King Tides peak over Thanksgiving
articles.summary: Coastal areas of California are bracing for potential flooding as king tides peak during the United States Thanksgiving holiday, with water levels reaching over eight feet in some locations on Wednesday and Thursday. The National Weather Service reported that these high tides are breaking records set just last month and are being strengthened by a strong El Nino weather pattern. Meanwhile, additional storm systems are forecast to impact the Pacific Northwest and the eastern United States.
articles.description: Parts of the Canadian province of British Columbia may also be affected by the storms and flooding, which come as millions of people travel for the holiday.

articles.headline: Maharashtra Cabinet approves free foodgrains for farmers and infrastructure projects
articles.title: Maharashtra Cabinet approves free foodgrains for over 42 lakh farmers
articles.summary: The Maharashtra Cabinet approved free foodgrains for more than 4.2 million farmers not covered under Direct Benefit Transfer across 33 drought-affected districts on Wednesday. Chaired by Chief Minister Devendra Fadvanis, the Cabinet also cleared a 55,48-crore rupee provision for the Narmada-Tapi diversion project in Nandurbar, established a separate MPID tribunal for financial fraud cases, and advanced the Maharashtra Private-Aided Schools Regulation Bill.

articles.headline: Election Commission directs states to correct electoral roll errors using Form 8
articles.title: ECI directs states to correct erroneous entries in SIR rolls through Form 8 during ongoing Special Summary Revision
articles.summary: The Election Commission of India directed chief electoral officers across twenty-five states and union territories on November 25, 2026, to rectify erroneous voter entries identified during the Special Summary Revision. Booth Level Officers will visit electors to verify demographic details and obtain Form 8 applications, ensuring no modifications occur through automated matching procedures.
articles.description: The ECI move follows complaints of incorrect entries in several cases in the final published SIR lists

articles.headline: Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade postponed to Saturday due to East Coast storm
articles.title: Storms push Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York City to Saturday
articles.summary: Organisers announced on Wednesday that the annual Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York City has been postponed to Saturday because of an East Coast storm threatening lashing winds and coastal flooding. Executive producer Will Coss stated that participant and spectator safety is the top priority for the 100th procession. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani confirmed that an expanded police presence will secure the route for the rescheduled holiday event.
articles.description: The parade, which marks its 100th edition, got a last-minute rain check ahead of heavy gusts on Thursday.

articles.headline: Zambian authorities ban planned protests over presidential term limit proposals
articles.title: Zambia bans protest against push to remove presidential term limits
articles.summary: Zambian police banned a planned November 25 protest against removing presidential term limits, citing clash risks with a rival pro-government youth group demonstration. The ruling party petitioned parliament to allow President Hakainde Hichilema a third term, drawing opposition from civil society and detained political figures facing disputed treason charges, though the government insists the president respects the constitution.
articles.description: Critics fear the campaign could undermine democratic safeguards as senior opposition figures remain behind bars.

articles.headline: Donald Trump expresses willingness to discuss Medicare for All with Democratic senator
articles.title: A meeting with Democrats over healthcare? Trump says he’s open to it
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump stated he is open to meeting incoming Democratic Senator Abdul El-Sayed of Michigan to discuss a national healthcare programme. While Trump praised the branding of a mock Trumpcare card shared online, no meeting date is set and he has not endorsed the proposal as Democrats prepare to take control of the US Congress in January.
articles.description: Experts tell Al Jazeera they are sceptical that Trump would back Medicare for All, a proposal for national healthcare.

articles.headline: Nato chief Mark Rutte vows alliance will defend against space threats
articles.title: Nato chief vows defence against space threat after Russian nuclear satellite reports
articles.summary: Following intelligence reports regarding a potential Russian nuclear satellite launch, North Atlantic Treaty Organization Secretary General Mark Rutte stated that the military alliance is prepared to protect its territory in space. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and European Space Agency head Josef Aschbacher also addressed the situation in Berlin, while Moscow dismissed the claims as unfounded allegations.
articles.description: German media said Russia planned to launch a satellite with a nuclear warhead into space in coming weeks.

articles.headline: Deadly truck fire is latest of Egypt’s transport disasters
articles.title: Deadly truck fire is latest of Egypt’s transport disasters
articles.description: Dozens were killed and injured when a truck carrying gas cylinders caught fire near Cairo’s Ring Road.

articles.headline: Jensen Huang returns as Nvidia CEO following brief resignation
articles.title: Was Jensen Huang too big to fire? Why Nvidia, Trump brought him back
articles.summary: Jensen Huang has resumed his role as CEO of Nvidia, the world's most valuable semiconductor company, just 11 days after resigning amid reports of extramarital affairs and a potential Chinese spy plot. His reinstatement followed intense pressure from the Trump administration and Silicon Valley figures, despite ongoing FBI, Justice Department, and SEC investigations into the company.
articles.description: Nvidia chief's 'mistakes' had consequences far beyond Silicon Valley. He is back nonetheless, in less than two weeks.

articles.headline: Andy Taylor, original guitarist for English new wave band Duran Duran, dies
articles.title: Andy Taylor, guitarist of new wave icons Duran Duran, dies at 65
articles.summary: Andy Taylor, founding guitarist of the 1980s English new wave group Duran Duran, has died at age sixty-five. His family and bandmates confirmed the passing in a joint statement, praising his musical impact. The artist had publicly disclosed in November 2022 that he was living with stage four metastatic prostate cancer during the band's Rock and Roll Hall of Fame induction.
articles.description: The band’s imperial stage occurred with a trio of hit albums between 1981 and 1983, with such dance-floor barnburners as ‘Girls on Film’ and ‘Union of the Snake’ and the moody ballads ‘The Chauffeur’ and ‘Save a Prayer’

articles.headline: Israeli air strikes kill seven in Gaza amid meningitis outbreak
articles.title: Israeli air strikes in Gaza kill 7 as doctors warn of meningitis outbreak
articles.summary: Israeli air strikes across the Gaza Strip killed at least seven Palestinians on Tuesday, including police officers and a child. Simultaneously, the Ministry of Health issued an epidemic alert, reporting a surge in meningitis cases to 272 in October. Health officials warn that deteriorating conditions threaten thousands of lives as the total death toll continues rising.
articles.description: Gaza health officials say meningitis cases rose to 272 in October, more than eight times the typical monthly rate.

articles.headline: Donyell Malen penalty secures Roma a draw against Paris Saint-Germain
articles.title: Malen and Roma deny injury-hit PSG in Champions League draw
articles.summary: Donyell Malen converted a late penalty to earn Roma a two-all draw against Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League on Wednesday at the Parc des Princes. The result halted the reigning champions' twelve-match winning run and their perfect record in this season's league phase. Mario Hermoso opened the scoring for Roma before Illia Zabarnyi and Ousmane Dembele scored for Paris Saint-Germain.
articles.description: Champions League holders Paris Saint-Germain held to 2-2 draw by Roma as injury-ravaged squad struggle.

articles.headline: Supreme Court rules speedy trial right does not guarantee bail for criminals with prior convictions
articles.title: Criminal with previous conviction can't be given bail only on strength of right to speedy trial: Supreme Court
articles.summary: The Supreme Court of India set aside a January 2026 order from the Punjab and Haryana High Court that had granted bail to an accused murderer who concealed a previous conviction for attempted murder. Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and Shree Chandrashekhar delivered the November 18 ruling, emphasizing that courts must balance an accused individual's right to a speedy trial under Article 21 of the constitution against societal and victim interests.
articles.description: "The right to a speedy trial is always considered to be a facet of Article 21 of the Constitution of India, but, at the same time, when the accused is involved in committing a heinous offence, the right of the accused and the interest of the society, including the interest of the victim and his family, is also required to be seen," says bench

articles.headline: Manchester United draw two-two with Sporting Lisbon in Champions League
articles.title: Man United denied at Sporting as referee overshadows Fernandes double
articles.summary: Mauricio Pochettino experienced a frustrating first match in charge of Manchester United on Wednesday as his side drew two-two against Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League. Bruno Fernandes scored twice against his former club, while Luis Suarez netted a brace for the hosts, aided by a decisive goalkeeping error from Senne Lammens. Youri Tielemans was also sent off late in the game.
articles.description: Bruno Fernandes nets twice in Lisbon, but referee's decisions in spotlight as Mauricio Pochettino denied first win.

articles.headline: Naval apprentice arrested for allegedly spying at Mumbai dockyard
articles.title: Trainee recorded 90 videos of sensitive installations inside Naval dockyard: Mumbai Police tell court
articles.summary: Mumbai Police informed a court on Monday that a 21-year-old Naval dockyard apprentice, Bunty Ramprakash Meena, recorded approximately 90 videos of sensitive military facilities. Arrested last week, Meena allegedly communicated with suspected Pakistani intelligence operatives via Instagram and WhatsApp. Authorities are currently investigating his contacts and potential financial transactions to determine the extent of the espionage network.
articles.description: Investigators are continuing efforts to establish the identities of other participants in the alleged group calls and ascertain the extent of the suspected information-sharing network, a Mumbai Police official said

articles.headline: South Korea issues air raid alert after Russian jets approach airspace
articles.title: Why S Korea issued air raid alert after Russian jets flew near its airspace
articles.summary: South Korea scrambled fighter jets and briefly issued air raid warnings for Ulleung Island on Tuesday after five Russian military aircraft entered its air defence identification zone. Although no Russian planes entered sovereign airspace, the alert caused confusion as authorities initially suspected a North Korean incursion. Seoul has lodged a formal complaint with the Russian military.
articles.description: South Korean authorities issue air raid warnings after several Russian jets were on verge of entering its airspace.

articles.headline: Google files patent for custom artificial intelligence video streaming feeds
articles.title: Google’s patent for custom AI video feeds paints a bleak picture of entertainment’s future
articles.summary: Google recently filed a patent for a system called My Channel, which aims to generate personalized entertainment using demographic data and large language models. Although the patent was rejected, the proposed technology would create tailored films featuring users as the main characters by utilizing their viewing history, location data, and contextual inputs from various connected streaming platforms.
articles.description: Last year, Google filed a patent for a system called My Channel that's designed to create feeds filled with personalized, AI-generated videos and advertisements based on information the company knows about its users. The patent has been rejected, but unfortunately, Google might appeal or resubmit an amended version, and we could see this monstrosity come […]

articles.headline: North Korea orders Swiss diplomatic representative to leave the country
articles.title: North Korea expels Swiss diplomat in sanctions row
articles.summary: North Korea ordered Switzerland's diplomatic representative to depart within forty-eight hours and closed the office following a dispute over Swiss sanctions targeting the Songdowon international children's camp. State media condemned the sanctions as a hostile act linked to allegations involving Ukrainian children. Swiss authorities stated that bilateral relations will continue through embassies in Bern and Beijing despite the diplomatic fallout.
articles.description: Swiss officials said relations would be kept through North Korea's embassy in Bern, and its own embassy in Beijing.

articles.headline: Russian air strike kills two in Zaporizhzhia following naval drone attack
articles.title: Russian strike kills two in Ukraine, days after ship attack off Libya
articles.summary: A Russian air strike on Zaporizhzhia killed two people and wounded over 40 on Tuesday, one day after Ukraine claimed to have sunk a Russian warship in Libya. Both nations launched hundreds of drones overnight, with Poland reporting a brief Russian drone incursion into its airspace. Russia continues to target Ukrainian energy infrastructure and Black Sea shipping.
articles.description: Russian attack on Zaporizhzhia destroyed a house and damaged a five-storey apartment building, Ukrainian officials said.

articles.headline: Supreme Court signals intent to stay high court order on civic polls
articles.title: Supreme Court suggests referring KMC delimitation case back to High Court for fresh look
articles.summary: The Supreme Court indicated it is inclined to stay a Calcutta High Court order that deferred municipal elections in Kolkata pending a challenge on ward delimitation. Justices emphasized that pending elections should not be postponed unreasonably. The Bench asked Solicitor General Tushar Mehta to seek instructions on the matter before November thirty.
articles.description: Supreme Court lists the case for hearing on November 30 after lawyers seek time to get instructions on the suggestion from the court

articles.headline: United States Department of Education investigates Virginia school closures
articles.title: US Education Department probes Virginia schools after sexual abuse scandal
articles.summary: The United States Department of Education announced an investigation and funding freeze targeting an Albemarle County district after local authorities shut down twenty-nine schools. Secretary Linda McMahon confirmed the enforcement action following revelations that over five hundred staff members missed routine background checks, though officials emphasized none are suspected of child abuse.
articles.description: Virginia schools face scrutiny after revelations of abuse and widespread failures in mandatory staff background checks.

articles.headline: Singapore agrees to US cooperation following Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia
articles.title: U.S. targets chip smuggling to China after Huang's return to scandal-hit Nvidia
articles.summary: Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong announced on November 24, 2026, that his nation will cooperate with the United States to prevent companies from rerouting advanced semiconductors to Southeast Asia and China. The development follows the U.S. Commerce Department adding Megaspeed International and several affiliates to its Entity List after Jensen Huang returned as chief executive officer of Nvidia following a brief resignation.
articles.description: Jensen Huang resigned over extramarital affairs, including with Alice Huang, linked to Singapore-based company Megaspeed International, who is suspected of being a Chinese spy

articles.headline: Voyager 1 becomes first human-made object to reach one light-day from Earth
articles.title: NASA’s Voyager 1 reaches one light-day from Earth on November 18: What does it mean?
articles.summary: NASA announced that the Voyager 1 spacecraft crossed the historic milestone of one light-day from Earth on November 18, 2026. Launched on September 2, 1977, the 49-year-old probe is currently travelling through interstellar space more than 16 billion miles away, with radio signals now taking a full 24 hours to travel between the spacecraft and mission controllers.
articles.description: NASA’s Voyager 1, humanity’s farthest spacecraft, is about to reach one light-day from Earth, more than 16 billion miles away; Know what it means

articles.headline: Bharti Airtel invests twelve billion rupees in Assam data centres
articles.title: Airtel to invest ₹1,200 cr in 3 data centers in Assam
articles.summary: Telecommunications firm Bharti Airtel announced plans to invest approximately twelve billion rupees to construct three data centres across Assam. The initiative includes a seven-billion-rupee facility in Guwahati alongside projects in Jorhat and Silchar. Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma noted that the development highlights growing investor confidence and will expand digital infrastructure in the region.
articles.description: All three data centers,Guwahati, Jorhat and Silchar, are expected to be in place by 2028

articles.headline: What’s behind Europe’s protests?
articles.title: What’s behind Europe’s protests?
articles.description: Increase in protests and industrial disputes across EU and UK.

articles.headline: Malaysia plans to repatriate over six thousand Rohingya refugees to Myanmar
articles.title: Malaysia set to return thousands of Rohingya refugees to Myanmar
articles.summary: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim announced on Tuesday that the country will return more than 6,500 Rohingya refugees to Myanmar through naval vessels and aircraft beginning December 6. The initiative follows a ruling by the International Court of Justice concerning Myanmar security forces and comes as Malaysia argues that hosting over 225,000 registered refugees has created an unsustainable financial burden.
articles.description: The announcement comes five days after the ICJ ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority.

articles.headline: VCK leader urges Tamil Nadu commission to enact anti-honour killing law
articles.title: Right to choose a partner is an aspect of constitutional freedom, not a privilege granted by a family, caste or community: Thirumavalavan
articles.summary: Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi founder and Chidambaram Member of Parliament Thol. Thirumavalavan submitted a memorandum to the Tamil Nadu Commission for the Prevention of Honour Killings, asserting that choosing a partner is a constitutional freedom. He urged the panel to recommend a comprehensive State law against honour crimes, establish a framework for mob violence accountability, and mandate official protection for couples.

articles.headline: Migrant wrongly deported by Trump leaves US for Spain
articles.title: Migrant wrongly deported by Trump leaves US for Spain
articles.description: Kilmar Abrego Garcia has arrived in Spain with his wife after a 20-month legal battle with the Trump administration.

articles.headline: Moment Nasa spacecraft hit asteroid - and what happened next
articles.title: Moment Nasa spacecraft hit asteroid - and what happened next
articles.description: The crash was "like something out of a disaster movie", the BBC's science editor Rebecca Morelle says.

articles.headline: Elderly man with Alzheimer’s rescued after 11 days in Amazon jungle
articles.title: Elderly man with Alzheimer’s rescued after 11 days in Amazon jungle
articles.description: A 74-year-old man with Alzheimer's has been found alive after missing for 11 days in Brazil's Amazon rainforest.

articles.headline: World Food Programme warns global trade route disruptions threaten millions with hunger
articles.title: Wars choke global food routes, threatening aid for 7.3 million, WFP warns
articles.summary: World Food Programme Executive Director Luke Lindberg warned the United Nations Security Council on Monday that disruptions across the Strait of Hormuz, the Bab al-Mandeb, and the Black Sea could increase operational costs by $727 million by mid-2027. Lindberg stated that these chokepoints threaten food assistance for 7.3 million people worldwide amid rising conflicts and climate shocks affecting global grain and fertilizer supplies.
articles.description: WFP Executive Director Luke Lindberg decries ‘political problem’ as grain is 'not reaching the people who need it'.

articles.headline: US Army destroys volatile lead azide explosives during Iowa military operation
articles.title: US Army declares Iowa lead azide detonation ‘tremendously successful’
articles.summary: United States Army officials confirmed the successful destruction of approximately 4,500 kilograms of deteriorating lead azide at an Iowa military base after a controlled detonation. Major General Eric Shirley stated the mission exceeded expectations with zero infrastructure damage. While Environmental Protection Agency sensors initially detected no airborne lead, independent experts emphasised the ongoing need to monitor potential environmental breakdown products and toxic risks.
articles.description: Army hails Iowa's lead azide disposal operation as some experts warn of potentially hidden toxins.

articles.headline: Donald Trump details efforts to reinstate Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO
articles.title: Why U.S. President Donald Trump believed he needed to get Jensen Huang back at Nvidia
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump confirmed his direct involvement in convincing corporate directors to restore Jensen Huang to his leadership position at Nvidia. Officials indicated the administration prioritised maintaining technological dominance in artificial intelligence and preventing foreign recruitment. Mr. Huang resumed his duties following a brief resignation sparked by personal conduct inquiries involving executive relationships.
articles.description: U.S. President Donald Trump has intervened to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia, following his recent ouster

articles.headline: Overthrown leader Sheikh Hasina plans return to Bangladesh on December 16
articles.title: Sheikh Hasina plans to return to Bangladesh from exile on December 16
articles.summary: The ousted former prime minister intends to travel back from Indian exile to Dhaka on December 16, according to her spokesperson Syed Mozammel Ali. Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's press secretary stated that the government expects her extradition as a convicted fugitive following her death sentence by the International Crimes Tribunal for orchestrating a deadly crackdown during the 2024 uprising.
articles.description: Hasina urges Dhaka to arrange her return on the national airline, as government says she can only be extradited.

articles.headline: Bangladesh government vows to arrest former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina
articles.title: Bangladesh vows to arrest ex-PM Hasina if she returns from India
articles.summary: State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam stated that Bangladesh will arrest former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina upon her planned return in December 2026. Dhaka is currently seeking her extradition from India under an existing treaty. Ms Hasina faces a death sentence following a 2024 uprising, prompting renewed street protests and clashes across multiple districts by supporters of her banned Awami League political party.
articles.description: State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam said Dhaka expects India to honour the extradition treaty, as Sheikh Hasina’s planned December return fuels political tension and street violence

articles.headline: D. Gukesh faces Javokhir Sindarov in World chess championship
articles.title: World chess championship: Gukesh to open title defence with black
articles.summary: Defending champion D. Gukesh will play with black pieces in the opening game of the World chess championship against challenger Javokhir Sindarov in Geneva. The best-of-fourteen match begins on Tuesday, following a colour draw at the opening ceremony. Gukesh acknowledged his rival's strong form and consistency, noting that the upcoming encounter will present a genuine test for his title defence.
articles.description: The first game of the best-of-14 match against Sindarov will be played on Tuesday

articles.headline: Six people killed in plane crash off the Mississippi coast
articles.title: Two children among six dead after plane crash off Mississippi coast
articles.summary: Six individuals, including two children aged eight and ten, died after a Cessna 210 aircraft crashed into the Gulf of Mexico off the coast of Mississippi on Tuesday. According to the United States Coast Guard, divers recovered the bodies from the fuselage after air traffic control lost contact with the flight traveling from New Orleans to Fort Myers.
articles.description: Divers found the bodies of three adult, one teenager aged 16, and two boys, aged 12 and 10, in the wreckage.

articles.headline: Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia highlights US-China technology rivalry
articles.title: What Jensen Huang's return teaches China's Xi about Trump
articles.summary: The billionaire executive's reinstatement as chief executive officer has drawn intense international scrutiny and sparked debate in Washington and Beijing regarding semiconductor export restrictions. Chinese President Xi Jinping is reportedly monitoring the situation closely as trade negotiations approach, while the United States Bureau of Industry and Security continues tightening rules on advanced computing access.
articles.description: Huang being back at the helm of Nvidia is no guarantee of relief for Beijing.

articles.headline: Saudi-led coalition launches renewed military strikes on Hodeidah port in Yemen
articles.title: Could renewed strikes on Hodeidah port worsen Yemen’s humanitarian crisis?
articles.summary: The Saudi-led coalition conducted new attacks against Houthi targets at Yemen's vital Hodeidah port on Wednesday. The escalation responds to recent Houthi territorial gains and missile attacks on Saudi Arabia. Handing critical commercial imports and humanitarian aid, the port has faced extensive damage from a decade of conflict and previous foreign military interventions.
articles.description: Disruptions at Yemen's largest seaport could exacerbate hardships for millions of Yemenis, aid experts warn.

articles.headline: British military relocates aircraft to hangars to guard against drone attacks
articles.title: UK military ‘moving aircraft to hangars in case of drone attacks’
articles.summary: Britain's Ministry of Defence is reportedly moving Royal Air Force planes into hangars and hardened shelters overnight alongside installing anti-drone nets. Security precautions follow warnings regarding potential sabotage and drone threats from foreign actors. The ministry noted it constantly adapts to counter emerging risks while investing heavily to strengthen infrastructure protection across critical military sites.
articles.description: Experts say the move is a 'logical response' if there is intelligence suggesting a likely drone threat.

articles.headline: Defending champion Gukesh faces challenger Sindarov in Geneva World Chess Championship
articles.title: Defending champion Gukesh starts as an underdog in World Chess Championships
articles.summary: Reigning world champion D. Gukesh from India is set to defend his title against Uzbekistan competitor Javokhir Sindarov in a best-of-fourteen match starting Tuesday in Geneva. Gukesh enters the contest as the lowest-ranked reigning champion since official Elo ratings began in 1971, following a ratings slump, while Sindarov arrives at a career-high ranking after winning the Candidates tournament.
articles.description: India’s world beater meets a fellow 20-year old challenger who is in his peak form

articles.headline: Jammu and Kashmir police target locals operating from Pakistan-administered territory
articles.title: J&K Police, after killing last local LeT recruit, shift focus on locals operating from PoK; properties of seven attached
articles.summary: Jammu and Kashmir Police attached properties belonging to seven individuals based in Pakistan-administered regions following the elimination of the final local Lashkar-e-Taiba recruit. Directed by police chief Nalin Prabhat under anti-terror legislation, authorities seized land linked to suspects who allegedly crossed the border during the nineteen nineties to support militant activities within the region.
articles.description: The police suspect that the accused crossed the Line of Control into Pakistan in the 1990s for arms and ammunition training and subsequently remained associated with efforts to revive terrorist activities in the region

articles.headline: Australia proposes multibillion-dollar fines for tech giants over online harm
articles.title: Australia warns tech giants of multibillion-dollar fines for online ‘harm’
articles.summary: Major technology platforms like Google and Meta face potential financial penalties of up to five percent of their worldwide revenue under legislation detailed by Communications Minister Anika Wells. The proposed digital duty of care law allows individuals to sue platforms for enabling wrongdoing, targeting serious harms including child sexual abuse material and terrorism promotion.
articles.description: New internet safety bill expected to pass this week could impose fines of up to 5 percent of firms' global revenue.

articles.headline: Surgeons remove large pancreatic stones through keyhole procedure
articles.title: Large-sized pancreatic stones removed via keyhole surgery
articles.summary: Surgeons at GEM Hospital removed large pancreatic stones measuring up to three centimeters from a forty-one-year-old male patient using laparoscopic surgery. Led by P. Senthilnathan, the medical team extracted the calculi without abdominal scars or stitches, providing relief to the patient who suffered from acute-on-chronic calcific pancreatitis and secondary diabetes.

articles.headline: Vehicle fire on Cairo ring road leaves thirty people dead and twenty-five injured
articles.title: At least 30 killed in Egypt vehicle fire, health ministry says
articles.summary: At least thirty people died and twenty-five others sustained injuries when a petroleum truck overturned and caught fire above a tunnel in Giza's Imbaba district on Wednesday. Egypt's public prosecutor launched an official investigation into the crash, ordering DNA collection from victims. Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly directed the state to cover all medical expenses for the injured.
articles.description: An additional 15 were injured in blaze after vehicle carrying petroleum products flipped on a major road.

articles.headline: Women commission urges special investigation into illegal egg racket
articles.title: Women’s Commission urges Telangana Governor to recommend special investigation into illegal oocyte racket
articles.summary: The Telangana State Women’s Commission urged Governor Shiv Pratap Shukla to recommend a special investigation into an illegal oocyte collection racket busted in Hyderabad. Chairperson Nerella Sharada briefed the Governor on the exploitation of vulnerable women brought from multiple states, highlighting legal loopholes in the Assisted Reproductive Technology Act.

articles.headline: Nvidia board and CEO face ongoing legal risks despite presidential backing
articles.title: Nvidia and board still face legal risks after Jensen Huang's return
articles.summary: State investigations in California and Missouri are proceeding into corporate governance and potential misleading statements following executive Jensen Huang's brief resignation. Although United States President Donald Trump asserted that the reinstated chief executive officer poses no national security threat, independent shareholder lawsuits and regulatory scrutiny regarding export controls remain active.
articles.description: Nvidia’s board reinstated co-founder Jensen Huang as CEO, pressured by U.S. authorities, sparked a rapid stock rally but left the company facing multiple investigations, including an SEC probe and a shareholder lawsuit over governance

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu officials association seeks fair inquiry into harassment complaint
articles.title: ‘Ensure fair inquiry into complaint by IAS officer’
articles.summary: The Tamil Nadu Indian Administrative Service Officers Association submitted a representation to Chief Secretary M. Sai Kumar requesting a fair inquiry into a sexual harassment complaint involving a woman officer. Police registered a first information report against Kallakurichi Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam Member of Legislative Assembly C. Arul Vignesh, while an internal complaints committee was formed.

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu opposes Cauvery water release decision at CWMA meeting
articles.title: T.N. opposes ad hoc release of only 2,000 cusecs at Biligundlu
articles.summary: The Tamil Nadu government registered its dissent at the 62nd meeting of the Cauvery Water Management Authority in New Delhi on Wednesday. Officials opposed a Cauvery Water Regulation Committee decision directing Karnataka to release only two thousand cusecs at Biligundlu for sixteen days, arguing that deficit years require pro-rata reductions based on yield assessment standards.

articles.headline: Colombian security forces storm Cartagena supermarket to rescue hostages
articles.title: Colombian police storm supermarket to free 76 held hostage for 17 hours
articles.summary: Colombian security forces freed approximately 20 shoppers and employees held hostage for 17 hours at a supermarket in Cartagena. Gunmen stormed the building on Tuesday following a failed robbery of an armoured car. President Abelardo de la Espriella authorized special forces to launch a rescue operation using stun grenades, resulting in the death of one gunman and the safe release of the remaining captives.
articles.description: One gunman was killed after what the country's president described as a robbery of a cash-laden armoured car gone wrong.

articles.headline: FIFA confirms United States and United Kingdom as 2031 and 2035 tournament hosts
articles.title: USA joint bid and UK confirmed as 2031 and 2035 FIFA Women's World Cup hosts
articles.summary: Governing body president Gianni Infantino announced that a joint North American bid led by the United States will organise the expanded 48-team Women's World Cup in 2031. Additionally, the United Kingdom will host the subsequent tournament in 2035 following an official rubber-stamping at a virtual gathering of member associations on November 23, 2026.
articles.description: The USA in partnership with Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica will host in 2031, when the tournament will feature 48 teams for the first time

articles.headline: Ousted Bangladesh prime minister Sheikh Hasina plans return on 16 December
articles.title: Bangladesh's ex-PM Sheikh Hasina says she plans to return on 16 December
articles.summary: Bangladesh former prime minister Sheikh Hasina announced plans to return home on 16 December, seeking air transport from Delhi to Dhaka. Living in exile in India since August 2024, she faces a death sentence in absentia for crimes against humanity. Bangladesh state minister Humayun Kabir dismissed her return terms. The announcement coincides with ongoing unrest linked to her banned Awami League party.
articles.description: Hasina has spoken several times of her desire to return, but this is the first time she has set a date.

articles.headline: Calcutta High Court defers final hearing on Great Nicobar Island project petitions

articles.headline: Nigerian President Bola Tinubu pledges security improvements at Maiduguri rally

articles.summary: Nigerian President Bola Tinubu promised supporters in Maiduguri on Wednesday that security forces would restore peace to the rebellion-hit border region ahead of the January 16 presidential election. Facing criticism over ongoing terrorism and kidnapping, Tinubu urged rebel fighters to surrender while security analysts noted improved accessibility across Borno State local governments.

articles.summary: The Kremlin rejected former British Prime Minister Boris Johnson's proposal to deploy a token Western military force to Ukraine, calling any foreign contingent unacceptable on Wednesday. articles.title: Iran says ships hit mines in Hormuz, warns vessels to coordinate passage
articles.summary: Two oil tankers struck naval mines and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz on November 25, 2026, after attempting to transit an unauthorized route.
