articles.headline: Brazilian president Lula da Silva won a historic runoff election after overcoming early adversity.
articles.title: Lula da Silva | The Pele of Brazil’s politics
articles.summary: Born in Pernambuco on October 27, 1945, President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva overcame extreme poverty and the loss of a finger in a factory accident to emerge as a prominent trade union leader during Brazil's military dictatorship. After facing decades of political attacks and arrests, he made history on October 25, 2026, by winning the presidential runoff following a second-place finish in the October 4 first round.
articles.description: The left-wing leader’s victory in Brazil, after finishing second in the first round, reflects the deep roots of the Workers’ Party, which built its support base through resistance to the military dictatorship in the early 1980s, as well as the declining appeal of Bolsonarismo

articles.headline: Brazilian President Lula da Silva campaigned across cities ahead of the presidential runoff.
articles.title: Lula takes to streets with people’s demands as Flávio leans on Big Tech in Brazil’s presidential race
articles.summary: Millions of supporters demonstrated across Brazil in mid-October 2026 to demand protections for public services ahead of the presidential runoff between incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and far-right challenger Flávio Bolsonaro. Capitalizing on widespread street mobilization, the Brazilian Senate approved a bill on October 15, 2026, to reduce the maximum working week to forty hours and guarantee two days of paid rest.
articles.description: In São Paulo, South America’s financial capital, around a million people marched last on October 18 with Workers’ Party banners and placards, demanding protection for public education, healthcare, and transport

articles.headline: Flávio Bolsonaro became the far-right challenger in the Brazilian presidential race.
articles.title: Flávio Bolsonaro | The Lula challenger
articles.summary: Flávio Bolsonaro entered the presidential race as the far-right challenger following legal difficulties faced by his relatives. articles.description: Former President Jair Bolsonaro’s son, running a pro-business campaign backed by evangelical groups, has emerged as a leading figure on Brazil’s far right

articles.headline: Russian governor Andrei Chibis detained in Murmansk corruption case
articles.title: Russian governor detained in rare criminal case against regional leader
articles.summary: Andrei Chibis, the governor of Russia's northern Murmansk region, was arrested in Moscow on corruption charges involving the alleged embezzlement of over one billion roubles earmarked for highway construction. According to the Russian interior ministry, the funds were siphoned off by a criminal group established in 2022, though Chibis denies any wrongdoing.
articles.description: Andrei Chibis, head of Russia's northern Murmansk region, is the first governor to be detained for five years.

articles.title: After six years apart, BJP and Akali Dal announce alliance for Punjab Assembly election
articles.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah announced on November 24, 2026, that the Shiromani Akali Dal has rejoined the National Democratic Alliance for the upcoming Punjab Assembly elections. During the announcement coinciding with Guru Purab, Shah stated that the Akali Dal will play the primary role in the coalition, which aims to eradicate drug abuse and corruption.
articles.description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi hails the move as ‘putting Punjab and the welfare of Punjabis first’

articles.headline: Wild indris in Madagascar use opera-like mouth movements to project songs
articles.title: What do lemurs and opera singers share?
articles.summary: Researchers from the University of Warwick and the University of Turin discovered that wild indri lemurs in Madagascar open their mouths wider when producing higher-pitched calls, mirroring vocal tract tuning used by human opera singers. The study analyzed 83 video recordings of 19 primates, revealing how convergent evolution enables these endangered mammals to project sound across dense rainforests.
articles.description: Recently, a study showed how indri lemurs use the same method opera singers use to ensure their vocals reach the audience at the back. In conversation with one of the researchers, Dr Chiara De Gregorio from the University of Warwick

articles.title: India AI funding nearly doubles to $1.6 billion in nine months of 2026: Tracxn report

Mumbai surpassed Bengaluru as the leading recipient city, driven largely by massive funding rounds secured by enterprises such as Neysa and Sarvam.
articles.description: Mumbai overtook Bengaluru as the largest recipient of AI funding in the country during the period, shows the report, which places India ninth among countries in terms of AI funding raised

articles.headline: Car bomb explosion in central Colombian city of Villavicencio injures 23
articles.title: Car bomb tears through Colombian city wounding more than 20
articles.summary: A car bomb detonated outside regional government offices in Villavicencio, Colombia, injuring at least 23 people and damaging surrounding buildings. articles.headline: Tamil Nadu government report identifies Thiruparankundram hill pillar as GTS survey marker
articles.title: What stands atop Thiruparankundram hill is a survey pillar, ascertains Tamil Nadu government report
articles.summary: A 2026 report compiled by Tamil Nadu's Departments of Survey and Settlement and Archaeology determined that the pillar near Sikandar Badusha Dargah on Thirupparankundram hill is a British Great Trigonometrical Survey marker. Published following an August 2026 Revenue Department authorization, the document confirms triangulation bearings match colonial records, providing clarity amidst ongoing disputes regarding local lamp lighting arrangements.
articles.description: This report has evoked interest against the backdrop of the latest dispute over the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam atop Thiruparankundram hill, which has taken centre stage, following the Supreme Court’s decision to permit the lighting of the lamp at the newly identified deepathoon as a limited, one-time arrangement

articles.headline: Nayib Bukele identifies three Salvadoran soldiers killed during anti-gang mission in Haiti
articles.title: Bukele shares details on deaths of El Salvador’s troops in Haiti
articles.summary: Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele announced that Lieutenant Cristian Daniel Palacios Santos and Corporals Emerson Alexander Zepeda Zelada and Wilber Manuel Serrano Medina died from an accidental explosion during an anti-gang mission in Haiti. Bukele stated families will receive 200,000 dollars and monthly income, while offering deployed troops immediate withdrawal without reprisal as multi-national forces combat armed gangs in areas including Martissant.
articles.description: Bukele's military intervention in Haiti comes after four Salvadoran technicians were kidnapped by gangs in October.

articles.headline: Democrats expand congressional majorities following midterm elections
articles.title: What could Democrats do with their expanding congressional majority?
articles.summary: Democratic lawmakers secured majorities in both chambers of the United States Congress following the conclusion of the midterm elections. The party holds 258 seats in the House of Representatives and 56 seats in the Senate, providing strong leverage to shape legislation and launch investigations during the final two years of President Donald Trump's current term in office.
articles.description: The Democratic Party is debating how best to use its large margin of victory in the US midterm elections.

articles.headline: Princeton researcher Eva Yi Xie detained by immigration authorities
articles.title: Chinese neuroscientist at Princeton is held by ICE after detention at Washington airport
articles.summary: Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers detained Eva Yi Xie, a doctoral student at Princeton University, at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport on Thursday. The Department of Homeland Security stated that Xie overstayed a temporary visa issued in 2016. Her legal counsel insisted that an asylum application provides valid permission to remain in the United States.
articles.description: ‘News of Eva’s detention is distressing for me and many members of the Princeton University community,’ Rodney Priestley, dean of the university’s graduate school, said in a statement

articles.headline: Borno school enrolment rises following years of conflict
articles.title: Borno school enrolment nearly doubles after years of conflict
articles.summary: School enrolment across Nigeria's Borno State reached 1,418,279 learners in 2025, according to state government figures. Authorities reported that regional reconstruction efforts and school repairs helped reduce the estimated number of out-of-school children following years of Boko Haram violence, although rural areas continue to face significant educational challenges and infrastructural shortages.
articles.description: Despite rising enrolment, violence, displacement and poverty keep children out of school in northeastern state.

articles.headline: South African father criticises police response after discovering daughter's murder on Facebook
articles.title: Dad who discovered daughter's murder on Facebook feels ignored by South African police
articles.summary: Tuku Nkosiyaphantsi learned of his 27-year-old daughter Okuhle's murder via Facebook after she went missing in Kokstad, South Africa. South African Police Service data recorded 581 female homicides between July and September, prompting nationwide concern over gender-based violence. While President Cyril Ramaphosa promised increased police presence and budget allocations, local communities have established curfews and patrols amidst ongoing frustrations regarding unsolved investigations.
articles.description: South African communities tell the BBC of measures they're taking to keep women safe after a wave of horrific killings.

articles.title: Mamdani blasts AI-reliant stock market after Jensen Huang’s return

articles.headline: Drone attack on Colombian police base injures three civilians
articles.title: Drone attack on police base in Colombia injures three, including infant
articles.summary: A drone strike targeting a police base in Cucuta, Colombia, injured three civilians, including an infant, and damaged sixty surrounding homes on Monday. Officials have not attributed responsibility for the incident, which occurred amid heightened military operations against rebel groups and drug trafficking organizations operating near the Venezuelan border.
articles.description: Far-right President De la Espriella steps up offensive as rebel groups strike back with drone strikes, roadside bombs.

articles.headline: European Commission proposes new sanctions targeting Russian banks and sports
articles.title: EU plans sports ban in sweeping new Russia sanctions proposal
articles.summary: European Commission chief Ursula von der Leyen introduced a sanctions package on Monday targeting sixty banks, crypto platforms, and Russian athletes in the European Union. The measures aim to maintain economic pressure nearly five years into the full-scale invasion of Ukraine. The proposal also includes visa bans for ex-combatants and requires approval from all twenty-seven member countries.
articles.description: Proposed sanctions aim to curb Russian crypto financing and 'propaganda' in sports.

articles.headline: United States plans to blacklist Singaporean artificial intelligence firm Megaspeed
articles.title: US to blacklist Asian AI firm Megaspeed after Nvidia scandal
articles.summary: The United States Department of Commerce announced plans to blacklist Singaporean artificial intelligence developer Megaspeed Ltd over alleged export control violations and ties to an industrial scandal. The company is suspected of helping funnel advanced Nvidia computer chips to China in violation of trade restrictions. Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang recently returned to Nvidia after scrutiny surrounding the firm.
articles.description: Megaspeed has been accused of funneling AI chips to China after a former executive's affair with Jensen Huang became public.

articles.title: Outrage after ICE arrest father and daughter at Seattle airport

articles.title: Trump postpones US Army plan to detonate toxic explosives in Iowa
articles.description: President Trump has further postponed the US Army’s planned detonation of nearly five tonnes of lead azide in Iowa.

articles.headline: Gisèle Pelicot announces legal action after nude photographs are distributed by book publisher
articles.title: Gisèle Pelicot 'humiliated' after nude photos sent to media to promote book
articles.summary: Gisèle Pelicot announced legal action against publisher Tinbad and author Sabine Prokhoris after intimate nude photographs taken by her ex-husband were emailed to media outlets to promote an essay on coercive control. The 73-year-old expressed deep shock at the commercial exploitation of her private life following her prominent 2024 trial. The publisher issued an apology, halting further print runs of the book beyond 280 existing copies.
articles.description: The publisher of an essay on coercive control apologises for "an unfortunate and inappropriate communication".
